017c5833-1a3a-4293-ab8e-132b51eb9b65.heading: Percentage yield of oxygen from 3.4 g of H2O2

beats.say: We start from 3.4 grams of hydrogen peroxide. Divide by its Mr, 34, to get the moles: 0.10 moles.
The equation says 2 moles of peroxide give 1 mole of oxygen, so the theoretical oxygen is 0.05 moles.
At room conditions one mole of gas is 24000 cubic centimetres, so 0.05 moles is 1200 cubic centimetres.
Only 480 cubic centimetres was collected. 480 over 1200, times 100, is a 40 percent yield.

024b76e3-72ff-4ab5-aad1-1ec2371e5b4f.heading: Purity of CaO from 27.8 g of CaCl2

beats.say: We work back from the product. 27.8 grams of calcium chloride, divided by its Mr of 111, is 0.2505 moles.
The equation is 1 to 1 for calcium oxide and calcium chloride, so 0.2505 moles of calcium oxide reacted.
Moles times Mr: 0.2505 times 56 is 14.03 grams of pure calcium oxide.
Purity is the pure mass over the sample mass: 14.03 over 40, times 100, is 35.1 percent.

0281895d-d722-482e-b61d-b5023cb7f932.heading: Heat absorbed per mole of NaHCO3

beats.say: First the Mr of sodium hydrogencarbonate: 23, plus 1, plus 12, plus three oxygens, is 84.
16.8 grams divided by 84 is 0.200 moles.
0.200 moles absorbs 6 kilojoules, so 1 mole absorbs 6 divided by 0.200, which is 30 kilojoules.

02fa979b-435d-409d-a532-ec5d7517c93d.heading: Mass of oxygen that combines with 6 g of hydrogen

beats.say: 6 grams of hydrogen, divided by 2, is 3 moles.
The equation needs half as much oxygen as hydrogen, so 1.5 moles of oxygen.
Moles times 32 gives the mass: 1.5 times 32 is 48 grams.

043261a8-ff12-4e53-8afd-45ef739f3f31.heading: Moles of Y in 7.8 g, from the oxide Y2O

beats.say: The oxide is 9.4 grams and 7.8 grams of it is Y, so the oxygen is 9.4 minus 7.8, which is 1.6 grams.
Moles of oxygen atoms are 1.6 over 16.
In the formula, Y to O is 2 to 1, so the moles of Y are twice that.
Moles of sodium chloride: 20 cubic centimetres is 20 over 1000 cubic decimetres, times 2 moles per cubic decimetre, gives 0.040 moles.
The equation is 2 to 1, so the theoretical lead chloride is 0.020 moles.
With an Mr of 278, that is 0.020 times 278, which is 5.56 grams.
Only 3.34 grams formed. 3.34 over 5.56, times 100, is 60 percent.

04e1577b-cc9a-4a65-8cb8-b944d16f0323.heading: Relative atomic mass of thallium from TlCl3

beats.say: The chloride is 15.2 grams and 10.0 grams of it is thallium, so chlorine is 5.2 grams.
5.2 divided by 35.5 is 0.1465 moles of chlorine.
The formula has three chlorines per thallium, so divide by 3: 0.04883 moles of thallium.
Mass over moles gives the relative atomic mass: 10.0 over 0.04883 is 204.8.

05238cfb-e68c-416d-a229-4e3f5d3024ca.heading: Molecules in 500 cm³ of oxygen at r.t.p.

beats.say: One mole of gas at room conditions is 24000 cubic centimetres, so 500 over 24000 is 0.0208 moles.
One mole contains 6.02 times ten to the twenty-third molecules, so multiply.
That comes to 1.25 times ten to the twenty-second molecules.

05266312-f5d5-4142-8274-efe2a3d1c336.heading: CO2 from citric acid and NaHCO3: which runs out?

beats.say: Citric acid: 1.92 grams over 192 is 0.0100 moles.
Sodium hydrogen carbonate: 30 over 1000, times 0.5, is 0.0150 moles.
The equation needs 3 NaHCO3 per acid, so 0.0100 moles of acid would need 0.0300 moles. Only 0.0150 is there, so NaHCO3 is limiting.
3 NaHCO3 give 3 carbon dioxide, a 1 to 1 ratio, so 0.0150 moles of carbon dioxide.
Times 24000 cubic centimetres per mole: 360 cubic centimetres.

05b1f5e7-c730-4a00-91f3-31b769e1f7ee.heading: Loss in mass when 33.6 g of NaHCO3 is heated

beats.say: 33.6 grams of sodium hydrogencarbonate over its Mr of 84 is 0.400 moles.
The equation is 2 to 1, so that gives 0.200 moles of sodium carbonate.
Times its Mr of 106: 21.2 grams of sodium carbonate is left.
The loss in mass is 33.6 minus 21.2, which is 12.4 grams.

099948ef-e520-476a-a518-1032b4bdd984.heading: Purity of the gold from the NO2 given off

beats.say: 10800 cubic centimetres of nitrogen dioxide over 24000 is 0.450 moles.
The equation gives 2 NO2 per copper, so halve it: 0.225 moles of copper.
0.225 times 64 is 14.4 grams of copper.
So of the 100 grams, 85.6 grams was gold, a purity of about 86 percent, not the 100 percent claimed.

0adcad6f-bec6-4f4e-8d67-ef854a814fc4.heading: Energy change per mole of KCl dissolving

beats.say: 4.0 grams of potassium chloride over 74.5 is 0.0537 moles.
720 joules for 0.0537 moles, so per mole it is 720 divided by 0.0537, about plus 13.4 kilojoules.

0b89d4c1-1c99-4f6a-9ed1-c5254531f8dc.heading: Which hydrocarbon has 1.0 g in 429 cm³?

beats.say: 429 cubic centimetres over 24000 is 0.0179 moles.
Mr is mass over moles: 1.0 over 0.0179 is about 56, which matches C4H8.

0e12c07a-bd0b-43b1-be07-e52826d6988d.heading: Volume of HCl from 50 cm³ H2 and 80 cm³ Cl2

beats.say: Hydrogen and chlorine react 1 to 1 by volume, so the 50 cubic centimetres of hydrogen is limiting.
It uses 50 cubic centimetres of chlorine, leaving 30 cubic centimetres over.
1 volume of hydrogen gives 2 volumes of hydrogen chloride: 2 times 50 is 100 cubic centimetres.

0fcd5bd1-41c0-479b-912f-fd1544ef29fb.heading: Salicylic acid for a 325 mg tablet at 70% yield

beats.say: The tablet is 325 milligrams, which is 0.325 grams. Over 180 that is 1.806 times 10 to the minus 3 moles of aspirin.
The equation is 1 to 1, but only 70 percent of the acid ends up as aspirin, so divide by 0.70.
That is 2.580 times 10 to the minus 3 moles of salicylic acid.
Times 138 gives 0.356 grams, which is 356 milligrams.

1086a677-848f-46ca-8839-dfd5643bf4ff.heading: Total gas after 90 cm³ NH3 meets 60 cm³ Cl2

beats.say: NH3 and chlorine react 2 to 3, so 90 cubic centimetres of ammonia would need 135 of chlorine. Only 60 is there, so chlorine is limiting.
60 of chlorine reacts with 60 times 2 over 3, which is 40 cubic centimetres of ammonia.
It makes 60 times 1 over 3, which is 20 cubic centimetres of nitrogen.
And 60 times 6 over 3, which is 120 cubic centimetres of hydrogen chloride.
Ammonia left over: 90 minus 40 is 50 cubic centimetres.
Total gas: 50 plus 20 plus 120 is 190 cubic centimetres.
10 grams of butanol over 74 is 0.1351 moles.
The equation is 1 to 1, so the theoretical bromobutane is also 0.1351 moles.
Times 137 gives a theoretical mass of 18.5 grams.
12 grams was made. 12 over 18.5, times 100, is 65 percent.

127af2d2-7a6a-418b-ba01-f2b72604cbd0.heading: Concentration of nitric acid from a titration

beats.say: Sodium hydroxide: 30 over 1000, times 0.5, is 0.015 moles.
Nitric acid to sodium hydroxide is 1 to 1, so 0.015 moles of nitric acid.
That is in 25 cubic centimetres, which is 25 over 1000 cubic decimetres. 0.015 divided by that is 0.6 moles per cubic decimetre.

12ed4216-78ba-4efc-b5ea-042561b59742.heading: Number of ions in 319.5 g of Al(NO3)3

beats.say: 319.5 grams over 213 is 1.50 moles of aluminium nitrate.
Each formula unit gives four ions, one aluminium ion and three nitrate ions, so 1.50 times 4 is 6.00 moles of ions.
Times 6.0 times ten to the twenty-third gives 3.6 times ten to the twenty-fourth ions.

14133740-b7c9-41be-83d8-207241e8bf9d.heading: Moles of X in 5.9 g of the oxide X3O

beats.say: The oxide is 5.9 grams and 4.3 grams of it is X, so the oxygen is 5.9 minus 4.3, which is 1.6 grams.
Moles of oxygen are 1.6 over 16.
In the formula, X to O is 3 to 1, so the moles of X are three times that.

14a91077-d7c5-4e34-b924-4d432ddb7f25.heading: Purity of pig iron from the hydrogen given off

beats.say: Moles of hydrogen are 1.58 over 24.
Iron and hydrogen are 1 to 1 in the equation, so the iron that reacted is also 1.58 over 24 moles.
If the whole 3.8 gram sample were pure iron, it would be 3.8 over 56 moles.
Purity is the iron that reacted divided by that, times 100.

14fb0c94-ceb4-4167-a08f-e7e2db82f075.heading: Oxygen atoms in 62.5 g of CuSO4·5H2O

beats.say: The Mr of the hydrated salt: 64, plus 32, plus 64, plus 90, is 250.
62.5 grams over 250 is 0.250 moles.
Each formula unit has 4 oxygens in the sulfate and 5 in the water, 9 in all.
0.250 times 9 times 6.02 times ten to the twenty-third gives 1.35 times ten to the twenty-fourth oxygen atoms.
8.0 grams of calcium oxide over 56 is 0.1429 moles.
The equation is 1 to 1, so the theoretical calcium nitrate is also 0.1429 moles.
Its Mr: 40, plus two nitrogens, plus six oxygens, is 164.
0.1429 times 164 is a theoretical 23.4 grams.
12.6 grams was made. 12.6 over 23.4, times 100, is 53.8 percent.

162e70aa-722a-4eed-b827-04c9a89d0704.heading: Gas left after 20 cm³ propene burns in 500 cm³ O2

beats.say: Propene to oxygen is 2 to 9, so 20 cubic centimetres of propene uses 20 times 9 over 2, which is 90 of oxygen.
That leaves 500 minus 90, which is 410 cubic centimetres of oxygen unreacted.
It also makes 20 times 3, which is 60 cubic centimetres of carbon dioxide.
On cooling the water condenses to a liquid, so the total gas is 410 plus 60, which is 470.

163deea4-5fcd-4b97-bfef-a57b0231217b.heading: Formula of a hydrocarbon from its combustion products

beats.say: 11.0 grams of carbon dioxide over 44 is 0.250 moles, so there are 0.250 moles of carbon.
9.0 grams of water over 18 is 0.500 moles.
Each water has two hydrogens, so 1.00 moles of hydrogen.
Carbon to hydrogen is 0.250 to 1.00, which is 1 to 4, so the formula is CH4.

17d5f14c-4b6f-4877-ab4a-5d00c2b5daef.heading: Purity of CaCO3 from 0.6 dm³ of CO2

beats.say: The gas is carbon dioxide. 0.6 cubic decimetres over 24 is 0.025 moles.
Carbon dioxide to calcium carbonate is 1 to 1, so 0.025 moles of calcium carbonate.
Times 100 grams per mole: 2.5 grams of calcium carbonate.
Purity is 2.5 over the 3 gram sample, times 100: 83.3 percent.

186e5324-c7fe-45ce-bf1e-cc1a053e677c.heading: Molecular formula from 85.7% C and Mr 56

beats.say: Moles of carbon in 85.7 grams: 85.7 over 12 is 7.14.
Moles of hydrogen: 14.3 over 1 is 14.3.
Carbon to hydrogen is 1 to 2, so the empirical formula is CH2, with an Mr of 14.
56 divided by 14 is 4, so the molecular formula is C4H8.

18e99fae-a92f-402a-88fd-e24d44574d33.heading: Gas from heating 14.85 g of zinc nitrate crystals

beats.say: The Mr of the crystals: 65, plus two nitrates, plus six waters, is 297.
14.85 grams over 297 is 0.0500 moles of crystals.
At room temperature the water is a liquid, so only NO2 and oxygen count: 2 moles of crystals give 4 plus 1, 5 moles of gas.
0.125 moles times 24 cubic decimetres is 3.0 cubic decimetres.

19897d88-284a-4bca-847f-c684584ca5ef.heading: Mass of CFC 12 from 10 g of HF

beats.say: We start from 10 grams of hydrogen fluoride. First, its relative molecular mass.
Mass divided by Mr gives the moles: 10 over 20 is 0.5 moles.
The equation says 2 moles of HF give 1 mole of CFC 12, so halve it: 0.25 moles.
Now the Mr of CFC 12: 12, plus two fluorines, plus two chlorines, is 121.
Moles times Mr gives the mass: 0.25 times 121 is 30.25 grams, about 30.3 grams.
Divide each percentage by its relative atomic mass. Carbon: 74.0 over 12 is 6.17.
Hydrogen: 8.7 over 1 is 8.7. Nitrogen: 17.3 over 14 is 1.24.
Divide by the smallest to get 5 to 7 to 1, so the empirical formula is C5H7N, with a mass of 81.
162 divided by 81 is 2, so double it: C10H14N2.

19b2db2e-d4ea-4c9a-bc14-c09cffe5d27a.heading: Purity of limestone from 10 dm³ of CO2

beats.say: 10 cubic decimetres of carbon dioxide over 24 is 0.4167 moles.
The equation is 1 to 1, so 0.4167 moles of calcium carbonate reacted.
Times 100: 41.67 grams of calcium carbonate.
41.67 over the 60 gram sample, times 100, is 69.4 percent.

19c0f81f-8db7-42e0-9fb4-6a70c77ba816.heading: Which element X reacts with 240 cm³ of Cl2?

beats.say: 240 cubic centimetres of chlorine over 24000 is 0.01 moles.
X plus Cl2 gives XCl2, a 1 to 1 ratio, so 0.01 moles of X.
Mass over moles: 0.24 over 0.01 is 24, which is magnesium.

1a1cf7c3-1e01-4c9a-ab76-f88667ccc387.heading: Purity of hydrogen peroxide from 3.6 dm³ of O2

beats.say: 3.6 cubic decimetres of oxygen over 24 is 0.15 moles.
The equation needs two moles of peroxide per mole of oxygen, so 0.30 moles reacted.
0.30 times 34 is 10.2 grams of peroxide.
10.2 out of 68 grams, times 100, is 15.0 percent.

1a35423f-d73f-45d7-9126-dfebe3b3da45.heading: Nitric acid from 0.50 mol of nitrogen

beats.say: Follow the nitrogen through. N2 plus O2 gives 2NO, so 0.50 moles of nitrogen gives 1.00 moles of NO.
All of that becomes 1.00 moles of NO2.
In the last step 4 NO2 give 4 HNO3, a 1 to 1 ratio, so 1.00 moles of nitric acid.

1a699db8-ed3b-435b-b644-ba0c8d034117.heading: Percentage of CO2 in 24 dm³ of air

beats.say: 10 grams of calcium carbonate over 100 is 0.100 moles.
Each mole of carbon dioxide precipitates one mole of calcium carbonate, so 0.100 moles of carbon dioxide.
Times 24: 2.4 cubic decimetres of carbon dioxide.
2.4 out of 24, times 100, is 10.0 percent by volume.

1a710bfa-e9d8-4a10-a4f0-c4b6a2bde3d6.heading: Relative atomic mass of Z from a silver nitrate titration

beats.say: Silver ions: 2.0 times 300 over 1000 is 0.600 moles. Each precipitates one chloride, so 0.600 moles of chloride.
ZCl3 has 3 chlorides per formula unit, so divide by 3: 0.200 moles of ZCl3.
Mass over moles: 32.5 over 0.200 is 162.5.
Take away three chlorines, 106.5, to leave 56.

1ad3e094-5231-4fd3-b9eb-b4b7c0570686.heading: Gas left after 50 cm³ of ethane burns

beats.say: Ethane to oxygen is 2 to 7, so 50 cubic centimetres of ethane needs 50 times 7 over 2, which is 175 of oxygen.
200 is supplied, so oxygen is in excess and 25 cubic centimetres is left over.
Carbon dioxide formed: 50 times 4 over 2, which is 100 cubic centimetres.
At room temperature the water is a liquid and does not count. Total gas is 100 plus 25, which is 125.
125 grams of zinc carbonate over its Mr of 125 is 1 mole.
The equation is 1 to 1, so 1 mole of zinc oxide should form.
1 times 81 is a theoretical 81 grams.
Yield is actual over theoretical, times 100: 75 over 81, times 100.
Take away the water to find the anhydrous copper(II) sulfate: 286 minus 126 is 160 grams.
Its Mr is 64 plus 32 plus 4 times 16, which is 160.
So 160 grams of it is 160 over 160, which is 1 mole.
Water has Mr 18, so 126 grams of water is 126 over 18, which is 7 moles.
The ratio of copper(II) sulfate to water is 1 to 7, so the formula carries 7 waters.

1e9bf080-db90-4d17-a0cf-b80c5916c90f.heading: Empirical formula from masses of C, H and O

beats.say: Divide each mass by its relative atomic mass. Carbon: 24 over 12 is 2.
Hydrogen: 4 over 1 is 4.
Oxygen: 32 over 16 is 2.
The ratio 2 to 4 to 2 simplifies to 1 to 2 to 1, so the empirical formula is CH2O.

1ea72121-a56e-4275-8ed4-54f0b3d5b0fc.heading: Percentage yield of ammonia from 60 kg of hydrogen

beats.say: 60 kilograms of hydrogen is 60000 grams. Divide by the Mr of hydrogen, 2, to get 30000 moles.
The equation gives 2 moles of ammonia for every 3 of hydrogen, so multiply by 2 thirds: 20000 moles.
Times the Mr of ammonia, 17, gives the theoretical mass: 340000 grams, which is 340 kilograms.
Percentage yield is the actual 60 kilograms over the theoretical 340, times 100: 17.6 percent.

1eb28e47-4e28-49f1-8a30-4a31a492b638.heading: Gas left when ethene burns in oxygen

beats.say: By volume, ethene to oxygen is 1 to 3, so 20 cubic centimetres of ethene needs 60 of oxygen.
70 minus 60 leaves 10 cubic centimetres of oxygen. All the ethene is used up.
Each volume of ethene gives 2 of carbon dioxide: 2 times 20 is 40.
Water is a liquid, so it is not counted. Total gas is 10 plus 40, which is 50 cubic centimetres.

1f7d4bbb-9021-4743-b336-584727319268.heading: Yield of carbon dioxide from heating NaHCO3

beats.say: 42.0 grams divided by the Mr, 84, is 0.500 moles of sodium hydrogen carbonate.
2 moles of it give 1 mole of carbon dioxide, so halve it: 0.250 moles in theory.
At room temperature each mole is 24 cubic decimetres: 0.250 times 24 is 6.00.
Percentage yield is the actual 4.50 over the theoretical 6.00, times 100: 75.0 percent.

209cbc51-a5e1-48d3-9567-2298a4c92203.heading: Gas volume from burning 0.2 mol of hexane

beats.say: At room temperature the water is a liquid, so carbon dioxide is the only gaseous product.
2 moles of hexane give 12 of carbon dioxide: 0.2 times 12, divided by 2, is 1.2 moles.
Each mole is 24 cubic decimetres: 1.2 times 24 is 28.8.

22a574ef-e8b5-4cea-be45-d2e3ba533dae.heading: Calcium chloride actually made at 85% yield

beats.say: 15.0 grams of calcium carbonate divided by its Mr, 100, is 0.150 moles.
1 mole of carbonate gives 1 mole of calcium chloride, so 0.150 moles in theory.
Times its Mr, 111: the theoretical mass is 16.65 grams.
Only 85 percent is actually made: 85 percent of 16.65 is 14.2 grams.

24143bdf-3e11-48b8-9f64-af51e9b4d6b4.heading: Oxidation state of manganese, same charge

beats.say: Copper first: 7.68 grams over 64 is 0.120 moles of copper.
Each copper ion is 2 plus, so the charge passed is 0.120 times 2, which is 0.240 moles of electrons.
The same charge deposited the manganese: 3.3 over 55 is 0.060 moles.
Electrons per ion: 0.240 over 0.060 is 4, so the oxidation state is plus 4.

2525c559-1877-4c9a-a273-55ebcb89f30e.heading: Yield of carbon dioxide from heating NaHCO3

beats.say: 42.0 grams divided by the Mr, 84, is 0.500 moles of sodium hydrogen carbonate.
2 moles of it give 1 mole of carbon dioxide, so halve it: 0.250 moles in theory.
At room temperature each mole is 24 cubic decimetres: 0.250 times 24 is 6.00.
Percentage yield is the actual 3.00 over the theoretical 6.00, times 100: 50 percent.
Find the mole ratio of salt to water. The Mr of magnesium sulfate is 24 plus 32 plus 4 times 16, which is 120.
12.0 grams over 120 is 0.1 moles of magnesium sulfate.
Water has Mr 18: 12.6 over 18 is 0.7 moles.
The ratio 0.1 to 0.7 is 1 to 7, so the formula carries 7 waters.

25f0f33a-d59d-420d-81e1-7da6b9329446.heading: Silver nitrate concentration from the precipitate

beats.say: The precipitate is silver iodide. Its Mr is 108 plus 127, which is 235.
1.18 grams over 235 is 0.00500 moles of silver iodide.
Check the iodide is in excess: 150 over 1000, times 0.05, is 0.0075 moles, more than 0.00500.
So mixture L held 0.00500 moles of silver ions, in 25.0 plus 25.0, which is 50.0 cubic centimetres.
Concentration is 0.00500 over 0.0500 cubic decimetres: 0.100 moles per cubic decimetre.

2973afe5-1d19-4761-be08-416d22445253.heading: Moles of X in the nitride X3N2

beats.say: Nitrogen makes up the rest of the mass: 102.0 minus 82.7 is 19.3 grams.
Moles of nitrogen atoms: 19.3 over 14.
The formula fixes X to N as 3 to 2, so multiply by 3 over 2.
70 grams of cerium over 140 is 0.50 moles.
It took 2 moles of electrons: 2 over 0.50 is 4 electrons per ion, so the ion carries a 4 plus charge.

299a028e-4651-4b50-af91-58d472c4ec17.heading: Gas left after burning ethane in oxygen

beats.say: 2 volumes of ethane need 7 of oxygen, so 4 cubic decimetres of ethane uses 4 times 7 over 2, which is 14.
16 minus 14 leaves 2 cubic decimetres of oxygen unreacted.
It also makes 4 times 4 over 2, which is 8 cubic decimetres of carbon dioxide.
On cooling the water condenses, so the total gas is 2 plus 8, which is 10.

29c79494-2419-4986-8189-e0e6a71dcc6d.heading: Yield of carbon dioxide from lead(II) carbonate

beats.say: Find the theoretical yield first. 42.0 grams over the Mr, 267, is 0.1573 moles.
The equation is 1 to 1, so in theory 0.1573 moles of carbon dioxide.
Times 24 gives the theoretical volume at room temperature: 3.78 cubic decimetres.
Percentage yield is actual over theoretical: 2.5 over 3.78, times 100, is 66 percent.

29fa1d16-4851-4f34-8e1d-61fe5c2cf3ab.heading: Concentration of sulfuric acid from a titration

beats.say: Moles of sodium hydroxide: 25.0 over 1000, times 0.100, is 0.00250 moles.
The equation needs 2 moles of sodium hydroxide per mole of acid, so halve it: 0.00125 moles.
Divide by the acid's volume, 20.0 over 1000 cubic decimetres: 0.0625 moles per cubic decimetre.
Take 100 grams of X, so there are 50 grams of each element. Sulfur: 50 over 32 is 1.56 moles.
Oxygen: 50 over 16 is 3.13 moles.
Dividing by the smaller gives sulfur to oxygen as 1 to 2, so the empirical formula is SO2.

2aa9e729-d858-41df-ae04-9231304f215f.heading: Most ammonium nitrate from 17 tonnes of ammonia

beats.say: 17 tonnes of ammonia is 17 over 17, which is 1 tonne-mole.
The ammonia is shared: 0.5 goes to stage 1 and makes 0.5 of nitric acid, and the other 0.5 reacts with that acid in stage 2.
Times the Mr, 80: the mass is 0.5 times 80, which is 40 tonnes.

2b02c767-bffa-4135-af56-68435c4e8b72.heading: Formula of a hydrocarbon from gas volumes

beats.say: Divide the volumes by 10 to get the ratio per molecule of X. Carbon dioxide: 60 over 10 is 6, so x is 6.
Oxygen: 75 over 10 is 7.5 moles of oxygen per molecule.
For CxHy the oxygen needed is x plus y over 4, so 7.5 equals 6 plus y over 4.
So y over 4 is 1.5, and y is 6. X is C6H6.

2c535be0-296a-4069-af14-284b6a5c62b5.heading: Charge on the titanium ion, same charge

beats.say: Copper first: 38.4 grams over 64 is 0.600 moles of copper.
Each copper ion needs 2 electrons, so the charge passed is 1.20 moles of electrons.
Titanium: 14.4 grams over 48 is 0.300 moles.
Each titanium ion needed 1.20 over 0.300, which is 4 electrons, so the charge is 4 plus.
Moles of lead(II) nitrate: 100 times 0.100, over 1000, is 0.0100.
Sulfuric acid: 50 times 0.100, over 1000, is 0.00500.
The acid is less, so it is limiting and fixes the amount of lead(II) sulfate.
So the mass is 50 times 0.100 times 303, over 1000, grams.

2dc0b977-3cef-4a0c-93af-dc8070775535.heading: Water to add to dilute sodium hydroxide

beats.say: Moles of sodium hydroxide: 2.00 times 20.0 over 1000 is 0.0400. Diluting does not change it.
The final volume needed is 0.0400 over 0.300, which is 0.1333 cubic decimetres.
The question asks for the water added, not the final volume: 0.1333 minus 0.0200 is 0.113.
Oxygen is the rest: 100 minus 18.5 minus 51.9 is 29.6 percent.
Moles per 100 grams. Calcium: 18.5 over 40 is 0.46.
Iron: 51.9 over 56 is 0.93.
Oxygen: 29.6 over 16 is 1.85.
Dividing by 0.46 gives calcium to iron to oxygen as 1 to 2 to 4, so the formula is CaFe2O4.
The oxygen makes up the rest: 100 minus 18.5 minus 51.9 is 29.6 percent.
Divide each percentage by the relative atomic mass. Calcium: 18.5 over 40 is 0.4625.
Iron: 51.9 over 56 is 0.927.
Oxygen: 29.6 over 16 is 1.85.
Divide through by the smallest, 0.4625: calcium 1, iron 2.00, oxygen 4.00. So the formula is CaFe2O4.

2f3996ba-d6ce-4014-86fc-497aed77664d.heading: Purity of sodium carbonate by titration

beats.say: Moles of acid: 20.0 over 1000, times 0.500, is 0.0100 moles.
The equation has 2 acid per carbonate, so halve it: 0.00500 moles of sodium carbonate.
Times its Mr, 106: 0.530 grams.
Percentage purity is 0.530 over 0.70, times 100: 75.7 percent.

2f8ad872-9afa-4ace-9384-24d29052a0aa.heading: Most fertiliser from 17 tonnes of ammonia

beats.say: 17 tonnes of ammonia is 17 over 17, which is 1 tonne-mole.
Stage 1 uses one ammonia to make the nitric acid and stage 2 uses a second to neutralise it, so 2 ammonia per ammonium nitrate: 1 over 2 is 0.5.
Times the Mr, 80: 0.5 times 80 is 40 tonnes.
Equal masses do not mean equal molecules, so go through moles. 2 grams of hydrogen, Mr 2, is 1 mole, holding x molecules.
2 grams of oxygen, Mr 32, is 2 over 32, which is 1 sixteenth of a mole.
So the number of molecules is x over 16.
Moles of bromine: 400 over 1000, times 5, is 2.0 moles.
So 2.0 moles of bromine react with 1 mole of the hydrocarbon: it has two C=C double bonds, one bromine molecule across each.
Each bromine molecule brings 2 atoms: 2 times 2 is 4 bromine atoms.
The Mr of aspirin is 9 times 12, plus 8 times 1, plus 4 times 16, which is 180.
So 0.20 moles of pure aspirin is 0.20 times 180, which is 36 grams.
Purity is 36 over 50, times 100: 72.0 percent.

344ef800-bf1a-448a-9410-0915ea1cea8f.heading: Percentage of ethanol in vodka by titration

beats.say: Moles of manganate(VII): 34.8 over 1000, times 2.0, is 0.0696 moles.
The equation has 4 manganate to 5 ethanol: 0.0696 times 5 over 4 is 0.0870 moles of ethanol.
Times the Mr, 46: 4.00 grams of ethanol.
Percentage by mass is 4.00 over 10.0, times 100: 40.0 percent.

363b5130-ae23-4bfa-b908-ee52a7d144ec.heading: Mass of oxalic acid crystals for a solution

beats.say: The water of crystallisation must be included: 90 for the acid, plus 2 times 18, is 126.
Moles needed: 0.1 times 100 over 1000 is 0.01 moles.
Mass is 0.01 times 126, which is 1.26 grams.

36f58320-2c63-48a3-8741-591c03b37464.heading: Carbon dioxide when the acid runs out

beats.say: Moles of calcium carbonate: 1 over 100 is 0.0100.
Moles of acid: 0.050 times 50.0 over 1000 is 0.00250.
2 acid per carbonate: 0.0100 moles of carbonate would need 0.0200 moles of acid, far more than there is. The acid is limiting.
Moles of carbon dioxide: 0.00250 over 2 is 0.00125.
Times 24000 cubic centimetres per mole: 30 cubic centimetres.

37883a92-a65a-4eef-ad75-335cbbb28265.heading: Sulfuric acid to neutralise sodium hydroxide

beats.say: Moles of sodium hydroxide: 0.100 times 1.0 is 0.10 moles.
1 acid reacts with 2 sodium hydroxide, so 0.05 moles of acid are needed.
Option C: 0.050 cubic decimetres times 1.0 is 0.05 moles, exactly right.
Moles of magnesium: 4.8 over 24 is 0.2.
Magnesium to magnesium oxide is 2 to 2, so 0.2 moles of oxide are expected.
Theoretical mass: 0.2 times 24 plus 16, which is 8 grams.
Percentage yield is 5.9 over 8, times 100: 73.75, about 74 percent.
1 methanethiol needs 3 oxygen, so 20 cubic centimetres would need 60. Only 30 is supplied, so oxygen is limiting.
30 of oxygen reacts with 30 over 3, which is 10 cubic centimetres of methanethiol.
That makes 10 of carbon dioxide and 10 of sulfur dioxide. Cooling condenses the steam, so water is not counted.
Unreacted methanethiol: 20 minus 10 is 10.
Total gas: 10 plus 10 plus 10 is 30 cubic centimetres.
Moles of lead(II) nitrate: 10.0 over 1000, times 0.10, is 0.0010.
Moles of sodium chloride: 30.0 over 1000, times 0.05, is 0.0015.
It needs 2 sodium chloride per lead(II) nitrate, so 0.0020 moles. Only 0.0015 is there, so sodium chloride runs out.
Left in solution: the excess lead(II) nitrate and the sodium nitrate formed.

3bba50fc-2d4a-4e44-8501-842f6a4f654c.heading: Mass of an equal volume of propene

beats.say: Equal volumes at room temperature hold equal moles. Ethane: 20 over 30 is 0.667 moles.
Propene has Mr 42: 0.667 times 42 is 28 grams.

3c1a2aae-3928-4802-88ff-3e9e48851380.heading: Dissolved oxygen by the Winkler method

beats.say: Work back. In step 3, 2 thiosulfate react with 1 iodine, so halve 4.00 times 10 to the minus 3.
By step 2 that equals the moles of MnO(OH)2.
Step 1 gives one oxygen for every two of those: 1.00 times 10 to the minus 3 moles.
Times 32 gives 0.0320 grams, which is 32.0 milligrams.
32.0 milligrams in 5.00 cubic decimetres: 32.0 over 5.00 is 6.40 milligrams per cubic decimetre.
Find the limiting reactant. The Mr of calcium carbide is 40 plus 2 times 12, which is 64, so 64 kilograms is 1 kilomole.
Water has Mr 18, so 54 kilograms is 3 kilomoles.
The equation needs 2 water per carbide, so 1 kilomole needs only 2. Water is in excess and the carbide is limiting.
1 kilomole of carbide gives 1 of C2H2, then 1 of C2H4, and every C2H4 unit ends up in the polymer.
The Mr of C2H4 is 28, so the mass of poly(ethene) is 1 times 28, which is 28 kilograms.

3ebf505f-f704-4e7c-8a54-e51032ee46af.heading: Identify X from the chlorine it takes

beats.say: Moles of chlorine: 240 over 24000 is 0.0100.
XCl2 needs 1 mole of X per mole of chlorine, so 0.0100 moles of X.
Relative atomic mass: 0.24 over 0.0100 is 24, which is magnesium.

3f03b9ca-e03a-4717-87f6-113a221f7b43.heading: Relative atomic mass of Z from its oxide

beats.say: Moles of oxygen: 0.233 over 32 is 0.00728.
1 mole of oxygen comes from 2 moles of Z3O4: 2 times 0.00728 is 0.01456.
Its Mr is 10 grams over 0.01456, which is 687.
3 times Ar, plus 4 times 16, is 687, so 3 times Ar is 623.
So Ar is 623 over 3, which is 208.

3fd83c39-0905-4cb5-a33c-5b1e4a9c03a0.heading: Relative atomic mass of M in M2CO3

beats.say: Moles of acid: 50 over 1000, times 2.0, is 0.10.
The carbonate to acid ratio is 1 to 2, so 0.10 over 2 is 0.05 moles of carbonate.
Its Mr is 6.9 over 0.05, which is 138.
2 Ar plus 12 plus 3 times 16 is 138, that is 2 Ar plus 60 equals 138.
So 2 Ar is 78 and Ar is 39.
The Mr of potassium carbonate is 2 times 39, plus 12, plus 3 times 16, which is 138.
41.4 grams over 138 is 0.300 moles.
Each mole of carbonate gives 2 of potassium chloride: 0.600 moles in theory.
The Mr of potassium chloride is 39 plus 35.5, which is 74.5.
Theoretical mass: 0.600 times 74.5 is 44.7 grams.
Percentage yield is 20.5 over 44.7, times 100: 45.9 percent.

429fcaa2-8fee-40ce-a52f-03d621f453ec.heading: Hydrocarbon from its mass and gas volume

beats.say: Moles of gas: 6 over 24 is 0.25.
So the relative molecular mass is 7.5 over 0.25, which is 30. Of the options only C2H6 has Mr 30.
The trophy gained 53.00 minus 50.00, which is 3.00 grams of copper.
Moles of copper: 3.00 over 64 is 0.0469.
Each copper ion takes 2 electrons: 2 times 0.0469 is 0.0938 moles of electrons.

42d48251-3467-437f-b741-c0262614132c.heading: Gas left after burning 10 cm³ of ethene

beats.say: 10 cubic centimetres of ethene uses 3 times as much oxygen: 30.
It gives twice as much carbon dioxide: 20.
Oxygen left over: 100 minus 30 is 70.
Water is a liquid at room conditions, so the final volume is 20 plus 70, which is 90.

4383ecc5-6e34-4113-8277-be14d592f75f.heading: 40 cm³ of ethane burnt in 210 cm³ of oxygen

beats.say: The equation says 2 volumes of ethane need 7 volumes of oxygen. So 40 cubic centimetres of ethane needs 140.
There are 210 cubic centimetres of oxygen, more than 140, so oxygen is in excess and ethane is limiting.
Carbon dioxide to ethane is 4 to 2, so the volume of carbon dioxide is 2 times 40, which is 80 cubic centimetres.

446318eb-f213-4c5e-a18a-6fb00df7e5aa.heading: Iodine molecules in 127 g of iodine

beats.say: 71 grams of chlorine is exactly 1 mole, since the Mr of Cl2 is 71. So 1 mole holds Y molecules.
For iodine, the Mr of I2 is 254.
127 divided by 254 is 0.5 moles.
Half a mole holds half as many molecules: 0.5 Y.

449b3a6f-461a-41f7-9caa-ad79428eb1fc.heading: Mass of Li2O from a titration with H2SO4

beats.say: Moles of sulfuric acid: 30.0 over 1000, times 0.5, is 0.015 moles.
That needs 0.030 moles of lithium hydroxide.
Which comes from 0.015 moles of lithium oxide in the 25.0 cubic centimetre portion.
The full 250 cubic centimetres holds ten times that: 0.15 moles.
With Mr 30, the mass is 0.15 times 30, which is 4.5 grams.

450a8e8c-940f-49ba-ac1b-537c23da6083.heading: Moles of HNO3 from 50 dm³ of oxygen

beats.say: Moles of oxygen: 50 over 24 is 2.083 moles.
Stage 1 gives 4 NO for every 5 oxygen, so 2.083 times 4 over 5 is 1.667 moles of NO.
In stage 2 this becomes 1.667 moles of NO2.
Stage 3 gives 2 nitric acid per 3 NO2, so 1.667 times 2 over 3 is 1.11 moles.

4548909f-e9e6-45c1-9c8e-6ac655b77e28.heading: Which sample has the most atoms?

beats.say: For each, work out the moles, then multiply by the atoms in one formula unit. A: 33 over 44 is 0.75 moles, times 3 atoms is 2.25.
B: 2 over 4 is 0.5 moles of helium, times 1 is 0.5.
C: 27 over 38 is 0.71 moles of fluorine, times 2 is 1.42.
D: 40 over 40 is 1.0 mole of magnesium oxide, times 2 is 2.0.
A has the most: 2.25 moles of atoms.

48b1dfc7-0be2-48d0-9740-957eda68edce.heading: 10 g of metal: most electrons in the sea

beats.say: Count moles of atoms, then multiply by the electrons each atom gives up. Aluminium: 10 over 27 is 0.370 moles, times 3 is 1.11.
Lithium: 10 over 7 is 1.43 moles, times 1 is 1.43.
Magnesium: 10 over 24 is 0.417 moles, times 2 is 0.83.
Sodium: 10 over 23 is 0.435 moles, times 1 is 0.435.
Lithium gives the largest amount, because it is by far the lightest.

4930e041-4e6b-4b8e-afab-9a3a91851875.heading: Enthalpy change for 60 dm³ of propane

beats.say: Moles of propane: 60 over 24 is 2.5 moles.
Each mole gives minus 2220 kilojoules, so 2.5 times minus 2220 is minus 5550 kilojoules.
The Mr of copper nitrate: 64, plus 2 times 14 plus 48, is 188.
The water, 18x, is 36.5 percent of the total.
Multiply out: 18x equals 68.6 plus 6.57x.
Collect the x terms: 11.43x equals 68.6.
So x is 6.

49be7639-73f7-47d1-811a-cebe65a9d665.heading: Concentration of sulfuric acid by titration

beats.say: Moles of sodium hydroxide: 30 over 1000, times 0.100, is 0.00300 moles.
The equation needs 2 sodium hydroxide per acid, so halve it: 0.00150 moles of acid.
Concentration: 0.00150 over 0.0250 is 0.0600 moles per cubic decimetre.

4b2e1771-d59d-4a86-84e7-696d1d4ae86a.heading: Empirical formula of an oxide of bismuth

beats.say: Mass of oxygen: 5.0 minus 4.48 is 0.52 grams.
Moles of bismuth: 4.48 over 209 is 0.0214 moles.
Moles of oxygen: 0.52 over 16 is 0.0325 moles.
The ratio bismuth to oxygen is 1 to 1.52, which is 2 to 3. So the formula is Bi2O3.

4bdce2a1-8475-4866-81c4-04026c5c98f0.heading: Mass of magnesium nitrate from 96 g of Mg

beats.say: Moles of magnesium: 96 divided by 24 is 4 moles.
The equation is 1 to 1, so 4 moles of magnesium nitrate form.
Its Mr: 24, plus 2 times 14 plus 3 times 16, is 148.
Mass: 4 times 148 is 592 grams.

4c583e0c-ca4f-4f2b-a81b-62398a9a7cb9.heading: Hydrogen atoms in 17 g of phosphine

beats.say: The Mr of PH3: 31 plus 3 is 34.
Moles of PH3: 17 over 34 is 0.50 moles.
Each molecule has 3 hydrogen atoms, so 3 times 0.50 is 1.5 moles of hydrogen atoms.
Number of atoms: 1.5 times 6.02 times ten to the twenty-three is 9.03 times ten to the twenty-three.

4d747169-77ab-4f56-80dc-b10366cdc3b7.heading: Grains of aspirin in a tablet

beats.say: Moles of sodium hydroxide: 12.25 over 1000, times 0.147, is 1.80 times ten to the minus three moles.
That is 1.80 times ten to the minus three moles.
Aspirin and sodium hydroxide react 1 to 1, so the moles of aspirin are the same.
Mass of aspirin: times 180 gives 0.324 grams.
Number of grains: 0.324 over 0.0648 is 5.

4dec360e-f1be-4301-97d0-625b98aded3a.heading: Which oxide of nitrogen is 0.23 g in 120 cm³?

beats.say: Moles of gas: 120 over 24000 is 0.005 moles.
So the Mr is 0.23 over 0.005, which is 46.
Mr 46 is NO2, so x is 1 and y is 2.

4e7b6b08-2085-41c2-a645-418c517dc266.heading: Mass of acid HA for 10 g of CaCO3

beats.say: Moles of calcium carbonate: 10 over 100 is 0.100 moles.
The equation needs 2 HA per carbonate, so 0.200 moles of HA.
Mass: 0.200 times 46 is 9.2 grams.

4fece9a2-38c3-46ab-a704-02b70510a610.heading: Percentage yield of iron from 80 kg of Fe2O3

beats.say: 80 kilograms is 80000 grams. Moles of iron oxide: 80000 over 160 is 500 moles.
Each Fe2O3 gives 2 iron, so the theoretical yield is 1000 moles of iron.
Mass: 1000 times 56 is 56000 grams, which is 56 kilograms.
Percentage yield: 49 over 56, times 100, is 87.5 percent.

504c3198-22e3-4772-9614-c8f120dfe146.heading: Which alkane needs 70 cm³ of O2 per 20 cm³?

beats.say: The ratio of oxygen to alkane is 70 to 20, which is 3.5 to 1.
An alkane with n carbons needs 3n plus 1, over 2, moles of oxygen per mole.
So 3n plus 1 is 7.
So n is 2. Two carbons makes Y ethane.

5258f95c-aa55-4e33-bc3e-33ee6c90054e.heading: Ar of X from 3.40 g of nitrate and 240 cm³ of O2

beats.say: Moles of oxygen: 240 over 24000 is 0.0100 moles.
One mole of oxygen comes from two moles of nitrate, so 0.0200 moles decomposed.
Its Mr is 3.40 over 0.0200, which is 170.
Subtract the nitrate group, 62, to leave 108 for X.

527206a7-f062-42e6-950b-c2e397de9aa2.heading: Volume of hydrogen from 2.30 g of sodium

beats.say: Moles of sodium: 2.30 over 23 is 0.100 moles.
2 sodium give 1 hydrogen, so halve it: 0.0500 moles of hydrogen.
Volume: 0.0500 times 24 is 1.2 cubic decimetres.
Divide each percentage by its relative atomic mass. Carbon: 52 over 12 is 4.33.
Hydrogen: 13 over 1 is 13. Oxygen: 35 over 16 is 2.19.
Divide through by the smallest to get 2 to 6 to 1.
So the formula is C2H6O, which is ethanol.

52818d82-a93e-400b-8089-82d56d8a58bc.heading: Volume of 0.500 mol/dm³ HCl for 18 g of Mg

beats.say: Moles of magnesium: 18 over 24 is 0.75 moles.
The equation needs 2 moles of acid per mole of magnesium: 1.5 moles.
Volume: 1.5 over 0.500 is 3.0 cubic decimetres.
That is 3000 cubic centimetres.

53c04f39-46c4-4c33-b812-4a88693eeed6.heading: Final volume: 20 dm³ H2 with 30 dm³ Cl2

beats.say: Hydrogen and chlorine react 1 to 1, so 20 cubic decimetres of hydrogen needs 20 of chlorine. Hydrogen is limiting.
30 minus 20 leaves 10 cubic decimetres of chlorine.
Hydrogen to hydrogen chloride is 1 to 2, so 40 cubic decimetres of HCl form.
The final mixture is 10 plus 40, which is 50 cubic decimetres.

55a6631f-c730-474f-9e6a-f8953c49f1fd.heading: Ar of X from 6.80 g of nitrate and 480 cm³ of O2

beats.say: Moles of oxygen: 480 over 24000 is 0.02 moles.
2 moles of nitrate give 1 mole of oxygen, so 2 times 0.02 is 0.04 moles of nitrate.
Its Mr is 6.80 over 0.04, which is 170.
Take away nitrogen, 14, and three oxygens, 48: X is 108.

577774b9-ef8c-4f18-9689-08d6bcdc756c.heading: Molecules in 0.3 dm³ of carbon dioxide

beats.say: Moles of carbon dioxide: 0.3 divided by 24 is 0.0125 moles.
Molecules: 0.0125 times 6.02 times ten to the twenty-three is 7.53 times ten to the twenty-one.
That is 7.53 times ten to the twenty-one molecules.

5af428ea-de34-45c5-973f-7252129aa806.heading: C=C bonds from the mass of iodine added

beats.say: The mass gained is iodine added across the double bonds. Per mole of oil: 25.4 over 0.025 is 1016 grams.
The Mr of I2 is 2 times 127, which is 254.
Moles of I2 per mole of oil: 1016 over 254 is 4.
One I2 adds to one double bond, so there are 4 C=C bonds.

5e5cccaa-0aa4-4440-9857-6c45e8aade5b.heading: Gas left: 10 cm³ CH4 with 25 cm³ O2

beats.say: Methane to oxygen is 1 to 2, so 10 cubic centimetres of methane uses 20 of oxygen.
So 5 cubic centimetres of oxygen is left over.
Methane to carbon dioxide is 1 to 1, so 10 cubic centimetres of CO2 is made.
The water is liquid. Total gas: 5 plus 10 is 15 cubic centimetres.

5e6e977e-b7f5-46ed-9f94-e86101d13951.heading: Salicylic acid for a 325 mg tablet at 70% yield

beats.say: Work backwards from the aspirin. 325 over 180 is 1.806 millimoles.
The equation is 1 to 1, so at 100 percent yield that needs 1.806 millimoles of salicylic acid.
The yield is only 70 percent, so more must be put in: 1.806 over 0.70 is 2.580 millimoles.
Mass: 2.580 times 138 is 356 milligrams.

5f13aa98-f861-4709-acb3-dfad581f77ff.heading: n in XCl2.nH2O from 10.8 g of water

beats.say: Moles of water: 10.8 over 18 is 0.600 moles.
Moles of the chloride: 0.100 moles.
n is the moles of water over the moles of chloride: 0.600 over 0.100 is 6.

5f415d2a-357a-4449-8e1a-a374e5e5ff06.heading: Formula of an oxide from its combustion volumes

beats.say: Divide the volumes by 20 for the simplest ratio: 40 to 60 to 80 is 2 to 3 to 4.
So the equation is 2 YxOy plus 3 O2 gives 4 YO2.
Balancing Y: 2x equals 4, so x is 2.
Balancing O: 2y plus 6 equals 8, so y is 1. The oxide is Y2O.

61866991-9507-47c5-9989-aff8ab692368.heading: Moles of X in 5.6 g, from 8 g of X2O3

beats.say: Mass of oxygen: 8 minus 5.6 is 2.4 grams.
So the moles of oxygen are 2.4 over 16.
In X2O3, X to O is 2 to 3, so the moles of X are 2.4 over 16, times 2 over 3.

62db1ae5-913a-450d-948f-9d310208caae.heading: Gas left: 20 cm³ propene with 150 cm³ O2

beats.say: 9 oxygen for every 2 propene, so 20 cubic centimetres of propene needs 20 times 9 over 2, which is 90.
There is 150, so oxygen is in excess and propene is limiting.
Carbon dioxide made: 20 times 6 over 2 is 60 cubic centimetres.
Oxygen left over: 150 minus 90 is 60.
The water is liquid, so the gas remaining is 60 plus 60, which is 120 cubic centimetres.

637897d3-444d-4a7f-9b65-0734f7564d27.heading: Purity of limestone from 6.0 dm³ of CO2

beats.say: Moles of carbon dioxide: 6.0 over 24 is 0.25 moles.
The equation is 1 to 1, so 0.25 moles of calcium carbonate.
Mass: 0.25 times 100 is 25 grams.
Purity: 25 over 50, times 100, is 50 percent.

6403a9b0-c5a6-4914-8cf8-2ea9979e803e.heading: Empirical and molecular formulae of P

beats.say: Divide each percentage by its relative atomic mass: 40.0 over 12, 6.70 over 1, 53.3 over 16.
That gives 3.33 to 6.70 to 3.33, which is 1 to 2 to 1.
So the empirical formula is CH2O, with mass 30.
The Mr is 60, which is 2 times 30, so the molecular formula is C2H4O2.

645794a9-1907-4dcd-a175-48bf31e6719c.heading: Formula of MClx from the volumes that react

beats.say: Moles of sodium hydroxide: 3.0 times 10.0 over 1000 is 0.030 moles.
Moles of the chloride: 1.5 times 10.0 over 1000 is 0.015 moles.
The ratio of chloride to sodium hydroxide is 0.015 to 0.030, which is 1 to 2. So x is 2.

649bed60-6267-47fe-89c6-70d273ad867f.heading: Gas collected: 70 cm³ butene with 300 cm³ O2

beats.say: 6 volumes of oxygen per volume of butene, so 70 would need 420. Only 300 is supplied, so oxygen is limiting.
300 cubic centimetres of oxygen reacts with 300 over 6, which is 50, of butene.
Carbon dioxide: 4 times 50 is 200 cubic centimetres.
Unreacted butene: 70 minus 50 is 20.
The water is liquid. Total gas: 20 plus 200 is 220 cubic centimetres.

676c6d13-1c94-466f-b09b-2f878a4a0809.heading: Shared electrons in the water from 0.5 mol propene

beats.say: Burning 1 propene gives 3 water, so 0.5 moles gives 3 times 0.5, which is 1.5 moles of water.
Each water has two O–H bonds sharing 2 electrons each: 4 shared electrons per molecule.
Total: 1.5 times 4 is 6 moles of electrons.
6 times 6 times ten to the twenty-three is 3.6 times ten to the twenty-four.

68d1b82d-8e71-4bfe-8757-389e9835ade7.heading: Water of crystallisation in two sulfates

beats.say: Iron salt: water lost is 3.97 minus 2.17, which is 1.80 grams, or 0.100 moles.
Moles of iron sulfate: 2.17 over 152 is 0.0143.
0.100 against 0.0143 is a ratio of 7, so x is 7.
Calcium salt: water is 2.88 minus 2.27, which is 0.61 grams, or 0.0339 moles.
Moles of calcium sulfate: 2.27 over 136 is 0.0167.
0.0339 against 0.0167 is a ratio of 2, so y is 2.

68fbe832-681c-4ef3-bd78-dbbcdb59c414.heading: Purity of a 23.0 g piece of chalk

beats.say: Mass of pure calcium carbonate: 0.226 times 100 is 22.6 grams.
Percentage purity: 22.6 over 23.0, times 100, is 98.3 percent.

6945916a-0cbc-477a-9219-adcc82849e58.heading: Purity of zinc oxide from 52.0 g of zinc

beats.say: Moles of zinc: 52.0 over 65 is 0.800 moles.
2 zinc oxide give 2 zinc, so 0.800 moles of pure zinc oxide.
Mass: 0.800 times 65 plus 16 is 64.8 grams.
Purity: 64.8 over 81.0, times 100, is 80.0 percent.

69e8d846-bfa1-48da-b271-c15028eb1c5b.heading: Moles of nitric acid from 50.0 dm³ of oxygen

beats.say: Start with the oxygen. 50.0 cubic decimetres divided by 24 gives 2.083 moles.
Stage 1: 5 moles of oxygen give 4 moles of NO, so multiply by 4 over 5. That is 1.667 moles.
Stage 2: NO and NO2 are in a 1 to 1 ratio, so there are 1.667 moles of NO2.
Stage 3: 3 moles of NO2 give 2 moles of nitric acid, so multiply by 2 over 3. That is 1.11 moles.
Start from the 13.3 grams of calcium nitrate. Its Mr is 40, plus 2 nitrogens, plus 6 oxygens: 164.
Mass divided by Mr: 13.3 over 164 is 0.08110 moles of calcium nitrate.
The equation is 1 to 1, so 0.08110 moles of calcium oxide reacted.
Mass of calcium oxide: 0.0811 times 56 is 4.54 grams.
Percentage purity: 4.54 out of the 7.00 grams, times 100, which is about 65.0 percent.
Moles of methane: the mass divided by 16 gives 5.00 times 10 to the minus 4 moles.
Follow the hydrogen through both steps: 3 from the first, and 1 more from the carbon monoxide. That is 4 per methane.
So the moles of hydrogen are 4 times 5.00 times 10 to the minus 4, which is 2.00 times 10 to the minus 3.
Multiply by the Avogadro constant to count the molecules.

6cace18c-a1c3-4d98-85db-ea007e1ab676.heading: Moles of Y in 11.2 g from the oxide Y₂O₃

beats.say: The oxide is 16.0 grams and 11.2 grams of it is Y, so the oxygen is 16.0 minus 11.2, which is 4.8 grams.
Moles of oxygen atoms: 4.8 divided by 16.
In Y2O3 the ratio of Y to O is 2 to 3, so multiply by 2 over 3.

6db3dd10-aebe-45f1-891b-dce038c318ab.heading: Sodium needed to make 48 g of titanium

beats.say: Moles of titanium: 48 grams divided by 48 is 1.00 mole.
The equation shows 4 sodium per titanium, so 4 times 1.00 is 4.00 moles of sodium.
Mass of sodium: 4.00 times 23 is 92 grams.

6f1eb543-f596-4dbc-a7e3-b8b17306df9f.heading: Hydrogen from zinc and nitric acid — limiting acid

beats.say: Moles of zinc: 1.3 divided by 65 is 0.0200 moles.
Moles of nitric acid: 20 over 1000, times 0.8, is 0.0160 moles.
The zinc would need twice its moles of acid, 0.0400 moles. Only 0.0160 is there, so the acid is limiting.
2 moles of acid give 1 mole of hydrogen: 0.0160 divided by 2 is 0.00800 moles.
Volume: 0.00800 times 24 is 0.192 cubic decimetres, which is 192 cubic centimetres.

7006764a-8405-406e-8f99-9ed2ff046742.heading: Ammonium nitrate from 17 tonnes of ammonia

beats.say: 17 tonnes is 17 million grams. Divided by 17 gives 1 million moles of ammonia.
Each ammonium nitrate needs 2 ammonia, one in each step, so halve it: 500000 moles.
The Mr of ammonium nitrate: 2 nitrogens, 4 hydrogens and 3 oxygens make 80.
Mass: 500000 times 80 is 40 million grams, which is 40 tonnes.

75070aa4-475d-4858-8dd1-6c7fc64e33f8.heading: Hydrogen peroxide for 0.239 g of lead(II) sulfide

beats.say: The Mr of lead(II) sulfide is 207 plus 32, which is 239.
Moles: 0.239 divided by 239 is 0.001 moles.
The equation needs 4 hydrogen peroxide per lead sulfide: 4 times that is 0.004 moles.
Its Mr is 34, so the mass is 0.004 times 34, which is 0.136 grams.

76414c66-2828-47d2-959c-36513be6b954.heading: Formula of sulfur vapour from equal volumes

beats.say: Equal volumes at the same temperature and pressure hold equal moles. 16 grams of oxygen, Mr 32, is 0.50 moles.
So 128 grams of sulfur vapour is also 0.50 moles.
Its Mr is 128 divided by 0.50, which is 256.
Each sulfur atom is 32, and 256 divided by 32 is 8 atoms per molecule.

76622b64-b14c-4274-b129-a606545bcce5.heading: Gas left after burning ammonia in oxygen

beats.say: 40 cubic centimetres of ammonia needs 3 quarters of that in oxygen: 30.
60 is available, so oxygen is in excess and 30 is left over.
The nitrogen made is 40 times 2 over 4, which is 20.
Water is a liquid at room temperature, so it adds no volume. Total gas: 30 plus 20 is 50.
Moles of zinc: 32.5 divided by 65 is 0.50 moles.
Each zinc ion takes 2 electrons, so the charge passed is 1.0 mole of electrons.
Moles of vanadium: 10.2 divided by 51 is 0.20 moles.
Electrons per vanadium ion: 1.0 divided by 0.20 is 5. So the ion is V 5 plus.

76a04e43-22f1-41e8-b11c-301f1af2f722.heading: Calcium carbonate with too little acid

beats.say: Moles of calcium carbonate: 10 divided by 100 is 0.10 moles.
Moles of acid: 100 over 1000, times 1, is also 0.10 moles. It needs 2 per carbonate, so the acid is limiting.
Only half the acid's moles of carbonate react: 0.050 moles, giving 0.050 moles of carbon dioxide.
Volume: 0.050 times 24 is 1.2 cubic decimetres, so statement 1 is correct.
Mass of carbon dioxide: 0.050 times 44 is 2.2 grams, not 4.8, so statement 2 is wrong.
Calcium chloride: 0.050 times 111 is 5.6 grams, so statement 3 is correct. Carbonate is left over, so 4 is wrong.

790969a9-8653-4842-9f53-fdbb60bc3997.heading: Iron(III) ions in 0.01 mol/dm³ iron(III) sulfate

beats.say: Iron(III) sulfate is Fe2(SO4)3, so each formula unit releases 2 iron(III) ions: 2 times 0.01 is 0.02 moles per cubic decimetre.
The answer is wanted in grams per cubic decimetre, so multiply by 56: 1.12.

79d4c519-d534-464c-bec5-26f4e4885de4.heading: Purity of ammonium nitrate from the water formed

beats.say: Moles of water: 30 divided by 18 is 1.67 moles.
2 moles of water come from 1 mole of ammonium nitrate, so halve it: 0.833 moles reacted.
Mass: 0.833 times 80 is 66.7 grams.
That is 66.7 grams out of the 100 gram sample, a purity of 66.7 percent.

79f53d8e-dd6c-4c45-bf39-478b54f7ac14.heading: Concentration of sulfuric acid from a titration

beats.say: Moles of sodium hydroxide: 25.0 over 1000, times 0.100, is 2.50 times 10 to the minus 3.
The equation needs half as much acid: 1.25 times 10 to the minus 3 moles.
Divide by the volume in cubic decimetres, 16.2 over 1000: 0.0772 moles per cubic decimetre.
Oxygen is limiting. 30 cubic centimetres of oxygen reacts with a third of that in methanethiol: 10.
That gives 10 of carbon dioxide and 10 of sulfur dioxide. The water condenses.
Of the 20 of methanethiol, 10 is left unreacted.
Total gas: 10 plus 10 plus 10 is 30 cubic centimetres.
Take 100 grams. Moles of carbon: 28.6 divided by 12 is 2.38.
Hydrogen: 4.8 divided by 1 is 4.8. Nitrogen: 66.6 divided by 14 is 4.76.
Divide each by 2.38: the ratio C to H to N is 1 to 2 to 2, so the empirical formula is CH2N2.
Its Mr is 42. And 126 divided by 42 is 3, so the formula is 3 times CH2N2.

7af411c3-5aca-432a-8614-81d3f96148e3.heading: Percentage yield of iron from 80 t of ore

beats.say: The Mr of iron(III) oxide is 2 irons and 3 oxygens: 160. The 2 irons in it weigh 112.
So 80 tonnes of the oxide can give at most 80 times 112 over 160, which is 56 tonnes of iron.
Only 50 tonnes was made. Percentage yield: 50 over 56, times 100, is 89.3, about 89 percent.

7b26f1d5-cf0d-44be-b539-aae938b2523f.heading: Nitrogen left from 0.120 g of urea

beats.say: Moles of urea: 0.120 divided by 60 is 0.002 moles.
The carbon dioxide is absorbed by the sodium hydroxide. Each urea gives 2 nitrogen, so 0.004 moles of nitrogen remain.
Volume: 0.004 times 24000 is 96 cubic centimetres.
Both stages use ammonia, one in each, so overall 2 moles of ammonia give 1 mole of ammonium nitrate.
17 tonnes of ammonia, Mr 17, is 1 tonne-mole.
Halve it: 0.5 tonne-mole of fertiliser.
The Mr of ammonium nitrate is 14 plus 4 plus 14 plus 48, which is 80.
Mass: 0.5 times 80 is 40 tonnes.

7c13c024-3755-4b84-8782-2b8a8c2257b9.heading: Hydrogen from 100 cm³ of 1.0 mol/dm³ acid

beats.say: Moles of acid: 0.100 cubic decimetres times 1.0 is 0.10 moles.
2 moles of acid give 1 mole of hydrogen, so 0.05 moles of hydrogen.
Volume: 0.05 times 24 is 1.2 cubic decimetres.

7c61ac72-9771-4722-86b7-f7d4943b0023.heading: Charge on vanadium from silver deposited

beats.say: Moles of silver: 54.0 divided by 108 is 0.500 moles.
Each silver ion needs one electron, so 0.500 moles of electrons flowed.
Moles of vanadium: 6.375 divided by 51 is 0.125 moles.
Electrons per vanadium ion: 0.500 divided by 0.125 is 4, so the charge is 4 plus.

7cef9a6b-68b5-4849-bf6d-602e8722e2a6.heading: Purity of calcium carbonate from CO₂ collected

beats.say: Moles of carbon dioxide: 360 divided by 24000 is 0.0150 moles.
The same number of moles of calcium carbonate reacted.
Mass: 0.0150 times 100 is 1.50 grams.
Purity: 1.50 out of 1.70, times 100, is 88 percent.
Moles of anhydrous magnesium chloride: 9.5 divided by 95 is 0.1 moles.
The water lost is 20.3 minus 9.5, which is 10.8 grams.
Moles of water: 10.8 divided by 18 is 0.6 moles.
The ratio 0.1 to 0.6 is 1 to 6, so x is 6.

7e67f7de-300a-4f74-a715-2babf6ff5a63.heading: Hydrocarbon from its CO₂ and water

beats.say: Moles of carbon: each carbon dioxide holds one carbon, and 1.10 divided by 44 is 0.025.
Moles of hydrogen: each water holds 2 hydrogens, so 2 times 0.45 over 18, which is 0.050.
The ratio of carbon to hydrogen is 1 to 2, so the empirical formula is CH2. Of the options, only C2H4 fits.

801657ef-2935-44ce-b913-267972b2b1be.heading: Mass of ammonium nitrate that gave 27 g of water

beats.say: The Mr of ammonium nitrate is 14 plus 4 plus 14 plus 48, which is 80.
The equation makes 2 waters, and 2 times the Mr of water is 36.
So 80 grams of ammonium nitrate gives 36 grams of water.
Scale up to 27 grams of water: 80 times 27 over 36, which is 60 grams.

8054271a-d4b2-4dd5-9f37-d0276aa33275.heading: Gas left when ethane meets too little oxygen

beats.say: 60 of ethane would need 60 times 7 over 2, which is 210 of oxygen. Only 140 is there, so oxygen is limiting.
140 of oxygen reacts with 140 times 2 over 7, which is 40 of ethane.
That leaves 60 minus 40, which is 20 of ethane unreacted.
It makes 140 times 4 over 7, which is 80 of carbon dioxide.
Water is a liquid, so it adds nothing. Total gas: 20 plus 80 is 100.
Moles of calcium carbonate: 450 kilograms divided by 100 is 4.5 kilomoles.
The equation is 1 to 1, so at most 4.5 kilomoles of calcium oxide.
Theoretical mass: 4.5 times 56 is 252 kilograms.
Only 170 kilograms was made: 170 over 252, times 100, is 67.5 percent.

81794f95-96f5-4bcf-bbd7-d152a415b660.heading: Which acid — from a titration ratio

beats.say: Moles of acid X: 6.0 over 1000, times 0.5, is 0.0030 moles.
Moles of potassium hydroxide: 22.50 over 1000, times 0.4, is 0.0090 moles.
The ratio of KOH to acid is 0.0090 to 0.0030, which is 3 to 1.
So each molecule of X gives 3 hydrogen ions. Only phosphoric acid has three.

81c99a0b-8c6b-488b-84f1-145eee5b5292.heading: Chlorine to react with 400 g of TiO₂

beats.say: Moles of titanium(IV) oxide: 400 divided by 80 is 5.0 moles.
The equation needs 2 chlorine per titanium oxide: 2 times 5.0 is 10 moles.
Volume: 10 times 24 is 240 cubic decimetres.

83822516-5e5b-46ce-b6c8-3a7d9b2aa09e.heading: Sulfate ions in iron(III) sulfate solution

beats.say: Moles of iron(III) sulfate: 2.00 divided by 400 is 0.00500 moles.
Each formula unit releases three sulfate ions: 3 times 0.00500 is 0.0150 moles.
The volume is 100 cubic centimetres, which is 0.100 cubic decimetres.
Concentration: 0.0150 divided by 0.100 is 0.150 moles per cubic decimetre.
The rest is oxygen: 100 minus 65 minus 13.5 is 21.5 percent.
Divide by the relative atomic masses. Carbon: 65 over 12 is 5.42. Hydrogen: 13.5 over 1 is 13.5.
Oxygen: 21.5 over 16 is 1.34.
Divide through by the smallest: about 4 to 10 to 1. So the empirical formula is C4H10O.

858eb5a7-cd03-4d96-88e5-0ed54d1455d5.heading: Purity of ammonium nitrate, set up as a fraction

beats.say: Moles of water: 28 divided by 18.
The ratio is 1 to 2, so halve it: 28 over 18 times a half is 28 over 36 moles of ammonium nitrate.
Its Mr is 80, so the mass is 28 over 36, times 80.
Purity is the pure mass over the 90 gram sample, times 100.

869713c8-ea4b-4053-b82d-c1e76d526803.heading: Calcium oxide in a mixture with magnesium sulfide

beats.say: All the hydrogen sulfide comes from magnesium sulfide, so there was 0.0250 moles of it. It uses 2 acid each: 0.0500 moles.
The acid left for calcium oxide is 0.125 minus 0.0500, which is 0.0750 moles.
Calcium oxide also uses 2 acid each: 0.0750 divided by 2 is 0.0375 moles.
The Mr of calcium oxide is 40 plus 16, which is 56.
Mass: 0.0375 times 56 is 2.1 grams.

870f7a66-bae3-4182-be47-d22195f01629.heading: Percentage yield of ethanol from bromoethane

beats.say: Moles of bromoethane: 10.90 divided by 109 is 0.100 moles.
The equation is 1 to 1, so at most 0.100 moles of ethanol: 0.100 times 46 is 4.60 grams.
Only 3.45 grams was made: 3.45 over 4.60, times 100, is 75 percent.

87b7ab0d-0ef9-4d44-b487-9100ea05e676.heading: Which carboxylic acid — from the hydrogen made

beats.say: Moles of hydrogen: 1200 divided by 24000 is 0.0500 moles.
The acid is monobasic, so 1 mole of hydrogen needs 2 moles of acid: 0.100 moles.
Mr of Q: 7.4 divided by 0.100 is 74. That matches C2H5COOH.

8843e85b-0cf1-4c85-9a9a-7bcddfa13f99.heading: Sodium hydrogencarbonate from the mass lost

beats.say: Only the hydrogencarbonate loses mass. 2 moles of it weigh 2 times 84, which is 168 grams.
They release carbon dioxide and water: 44 plus 18 is 62 grams lost.
So 1.5 grams lost came from 1.5 times 168 over 62, which is 4.06 grams.
Percentage: 4.06 over 6.0, times 100, is 68 percent.
The 2 to 9 ratio means 20 of propene uses 20 times 9 over 2, which is 90 of oxygen.
That leaves 500 minus 90, which is 410 of oxygen.
It makes 20 times 3, which is 60 of carbon dioxide.
The water is a liquid, so the gas left is 410 plus 60, which is 470.

89c0f121-a6fa-46c2-8582-b6d1e091f1e2.heading: Water to add to dilute sodium hydroxide

beats.say: Moles of sodium hydroxide: 25 over 1000, times 1.0, is 0.025 moles.
Diluting does not change the moles, so the final volume is 0.025 divided by 0.1: 0.25 cubic decimetres, or 250 cubic centimetres.
The question asks for the water to add: 250 minus 25 is 225.

89da0a1c-247a-4511-9bde-17c2c0a2af5c.heading: Nitrogen and hydrogen — which runs out?

beats.say: 1 mole of nitrogen reacts with 3 of hydrogen, so 2 moles of nitrogen needs 6 of hydrogen.
7 moles are there, so nitrogen is used up and 7 minus 6, which is 1 mole of hydrogen, is left.
Ammonia made: 2 times 2 is 4 moles.

8b133f2b-f055-4776-acb9-7c20dc8f1e78.heading: Concentration of ascorbic acid from one tablet

beats.say: Moles of ascorbic acid: 0.080 divided by 176.
The volume is 200 cubic centimetres, which is 0.200 cubic decimetres.
Concentration: divide the moles by 0.200. That gives 0.00227 moles per cubic decimetre.

8c7ff13d-f61a-4deb-9fd1-a760c5a0ca83.heading: Chlorine made with 2.00 g of calcium

beats.say: Moles of calcium: 2.00 divided by 40 is 0.0500 moles.
The ratio is 1 to 1, so 0.0500 moles of chlorine.
Its Mr is 71, so the mass is 0.0500 times 71, which is 3.55 grams.
Start from 18.4 grams of sodium. Divide by its relative atomic mass, 23, to get the moles.
The equation says 2 moles of sodium give 1 mole of hydrogen, so halve it: 0.400 moles.
One mole of gas at r.t.p. takes up 24 cubic decimetres: 0.400 times 24 is 9.6 cubic decimetres.

8dee6785-0fdf-439d-a6d1-d4286bfbf1c4.heading: Percentage yield of iron from its oxide

beats.say: Find the theoretical mass of iron first. The Mr of iron(III) oxide: 2 irons and 3 oxygens make 160.
80 tonnes divided by 160 gives 0.50, in tonne-moles.
The equation gives 2 moles of iron per mole of iron(III) oxide: 2 times 0.50 is 1.0.
So the theoretical mass of iron is 1.0 times 56, which is 56 tonnes.
Only 50 tonnes were made: 50 over 56, times 100, is 89 percent.
Moles of sodium: 4.6 grams divided by 23 is 0.20 moles.
From the equation, 2 moles of sodium give 1 mole of hydrogen, so 0.10 moles of hydrogen.
Each mole of gas is 24 cubic decimetres: 0.10 times 24 is 2.4 cubic decimetres.

9027023c-8c8c-404b-8782-cf296fff6546.heading: Ammonia needed for 60.0 g of urea at 80% yield

beats.say: The yield is 80 percent, so the theoretical mass of urea is 60.0 divided by 0.80: 75.0 grams.
Divide by the Mr of urea, 60: 75.0 over 60 is 1.25 moles.
Ammonia to urea is 2 to 1, so 2 times 1.25 is 2.5 moles of ammonia.
Mass of ammonia: 2.5 times 17 is 42.5 grams.

908dd7c5-1260-417e-9eff-4eea416388d5.heading: Oxygen needed to heat 194 g of zinc sulfide

beats.say: The Mr of zinc sulfide is 65 plus 32, which is 97.
So 194 grams is 194 over 97, which is 2 moles.
From the equation, 2 moles of zinc sulfide need 3 moles of oxygen.
At r.t.p. each mole is 24 cubic decimetres: 3 times 24 is 72 cubic decimetres.
Equal charge means equal moles of electrons. First the copper: 19.2 over 64 is 0.300 moles.
Copper is 2 plus, so the electrons passed are 2 times 0.300: 0.600 moles.
Now the scandium: 9 over 45 is 0.200 moles.
Electrons per scandium atom: 0.600 over 0.200 is 3. So the ion is scandium 3 plus.

9531b5d9-6e72-4bf0-a759-cb4cf471f2f0.heading: Empirical formula from percentages by mass

beats.say: Divide each percentage by the relative atomic mass. Carbon: 41.9 over 12 is 3.49.
Hydrogen: 3.1 over 1 is 3.10.
Chlorine: 55.0 over 35.5 is 1.55.
Divide through by the smallest, 1.55.
Those are not whole numbers, so multiply by 4: 9 to 8 to 4.

9542163a-3a6b-4a42-bd4e-8ce1c6cc788a.heading: Water from 8.0 g of hydrogen and 8.0 g of oxygen

beats.say: 8.0 grams of hydrogen is 4 moles.
But 8.0 grams of oxygen is only 0.25 moles.
By the equation, the oxygen is the limiting reactant.
1 mole of oxygen gives 2 moles of water: 2 times 0.25 is 0.5 moles.
Mass of water: 0.5 times 18 is 9.0 grams.

9566d0ad-4474-4399-a03b-ece0fc4da915.heading: Chlorine atoms in a volume of chlorine gas

beats.say: Change 480 cubic centimetres to cubic decimetres, then divide by 24 for the moles of chlorine gas.
Multiplying by 6.02 times ten to the twenty-three gives the number of molecules.
Each chlorine molecule contains 2 chlorine atoms, so multiply by 2.
The Mr of magnesium nitrate is 148.
23 grams of it is 23 over 148, which is 0.1554 moles.
The equation is 1 to 1, so there were 0.1554 moles of magnesium oxide.
Mass of magnesium oxide: 0.1554 times 40 is 6.22 grams.
Purity: 6.22 out of the 12 grams, times 100, is 51.8 percent.

9852dcca-920e-42f1-add8-b533ee99d9a3.heading: Volume of NaOH for 0.49 g of sulfuric acid

beats.say: Moles of sulfuric acid: 0.49 over 98 is 0.0050 moles.
The equation needs 2 sodium hydroxide per sulfuric acid: 2 times 0.0050 is 0.010 moles.
Volume is moles over concentration: 0.010 over 0.20 is 0.050 cubic decimetres.
That is 50.0 cubic centimetres.

987846e7-34c4-4153-adc5-d2efe4876d0e.heading: Mr of a gas from its mass and volume

beats.say: At r.t.p., 6 cubic decimetres is 6 over 24, which is 0.25 moles.
Mr is mass over moles: 7 over 0.25 is 28.

98ba58a7-cd2f-49f0-b57b-ae3b0e1dfc70.heading: Gas left after urea reacts with nitrous acid

beats.say: Moles of urea: 0.120 over 60 is 0.00200 moles.
The acid available: 0.0250 times 0.750 is 0.01875 moles.
Only 0.00400 moles of acid are needed, far less than that, so the urea is limiting.
Each urea gives 2 nitrogen: 2 times 0.00200 is 0.00400 moles of nitrogen, plus 0.00200 moles of carbon dioxide.
The sodium hydroxide absorbs the carbon dioxide, leaving only the nitrogen.
Volume of nitrogen: 0.00400 times 24000 is 96.0 cubic centimetres.
Moles of acid: 0.250 times 2.86 over 1000 is 7.15 times ten to the minus four moles.
Sodium hydrogencarbonate and the acid react 1 to 1, so the same number of moles.
Mass: times 84, which is 0.0601 grams.
Percentage: 0.0601 out of 1.00 gram, times 100, is 6.0 percent.

9a12a02b-5b2f-4a51-8f68-a5db15280b81.heading: Formula of an oxide with 68.4% chromium

beats.say: In 100 grams of the oxide there are 68.4 grams of chromium and 31.6 grams of oxygen.
Moles of chromium: 68.4 over 52 is 1.32.
Moles of oxygen: 31.6 over 16 is 1.98.
That is a ratio of 1 to 1.5, or 2 to 3.
Find the limiting reactant first. Copper(II) oxide: 20 over 80 is 0.25 moles.
Sulfuric acid: 100 over 1000, times 5.0, is 0.50 moles.
The equation is 1 to 1, so the acid is in excess and copper(II) oxide is limiting.
So the theoretical moles of copper(II) sulfate are 0.25.
Its Mr is 64 plus 32 plus 64, which is 160.
Theoretical mass: 0.25 times 160 is 40 grams.
At 85 percent yield: 0.85 times 40 is 34 grams.

9b4e08c3-f39c-44f9-9d53-79e7abed93f5.heading: Molecular formula from 0.10 mol of a compound

beats.say: Scale up to one mole by dividing each mass by 0.10. Oxygen: 48 grams.
Hydrogen: 16 grams.
Carbon: 96 grams.
Moles of oxygen atoms: 48 over 16 is 3.
Hydrogen: 16 over 1 is 16.
Carbon: 96 over 12 is 8. So the formula is C 8, H 16, O 3.

9b79c0f7-1000-469a-aca1-c55df5f7d3a8.heading: Limestone needed for 84 kg of calcium oxide

beats.say: The Mr of calcium oxide is 40 plus 16, which is 56.
84 kilograms of it is 84 over 56, which is 1.5 kilomoles.
1 mole of calcium carbonate gives 1 mole of calcium oxide, so 1.5 kilomoles of limestone.
Calcium carbonate has Mr 100: 1.5 times 100 is 150 kilograms.
Moles of boron: 0.78 over 11 is 0.0709.
Moles of carbon: 0.22 over 12 is 0.0183.
Divide by the smaller: about 3.9 to 1, which rounds to 4 to 1.

9bd38415-072d-47c0-8e49-f3351cb4a54e.heading: Volume of oxygen mixed with nitrogen monoxide

beats.say: Gas volumes react in the mole ratio. 20 cubic centimetres of nitrogen monoxide reacts with 10 of oxygen.
And it gives 20 cubic centimetres of nitrogen dioxide.
Gas left at the end: the nitrogen dioxide plus the oxygen not used, which totals 40.
So x is 30.
Moles of butanol: 10 over 74 is 0.1351 moles.
The equation is 1 to 1, so the theoretical yield is 0.1351 moles of bromobutane.
Theoretical mass: 0.1351 times 137 is 18.5 grams.
Percentage yield: 12 over 18.5, times 100, is 65 percent.
Moles of sodium hydrogencarbonate: 42.0 over 84 is 0.500 moles.
2 moles give 1 mole of carbon dioxide, so the theoretical moles are 0.250.
As a volume: 0.250 times 24 is 6.00 cubic decimetres.
Only 3.00 were released: 3.00 over 6.00, times 100, is 50 percent.

9d1ee7a8-df08-464d-9b8f-4d15f72af569.heading: Concentration of KOH from a titration

beats.say: Moles of sulfuric acid: 15.0 over 1000, times 0.20, is 3.0 times ten to the minus three.
Neutralising it needs twice as much potassium hydroxide: 6.0 times ten to the minus three moles.
Concentration: divide by the volume, 30.0 over 1000 cubic decimetres. That gives 0.20.
Moles of cyanogen: 0.600 cubic decimetres over 24 is 0.0250 moles.
Mr is mass over moles: 1.3 over 0.0250 is 52.
The empirical formula CN has a mass of 12 plus 14, which is 26.
52 over 26 is 2, so the molecular formula is C 2 N 2.

9e458a36-4e1b-4624-8985-b5db376efb3d.heading: Magnesium chloride from 48.0 g of magnesium

beats.say: Moles of magnesium: 48.0 over 24 is 2.00 moles.
The equation gives one mole of magnesium chloride per mole of magnesium.
Its Mr is 24 plus 71, which is 95.
Mass: 2.00 times 95 is 190 grams.
Only zinc reacts. Moles of hydrogen: 1.85 over 24 is 0.0771 moles.
So the moles of zinc are also 0.0771.
Mass of zinc: 0.0771 times 65 is 5.01 grams.
Zinc is 5.01 out of 24.0 grams, which is 20.9 percent.
The rest is copper: 100 minus 20.9 is 79.1 percent.

9ea25cdb-8129-4b13-9e25-b405f9846995.heading: Anhydrous zinc sulfate from 44.0 g of oxygen

beats.say: The hydrated crystal contains 11 oxygen atoms: 4 in the sulfate and 7 in the water.
Moles of oxygen atoms: 44.0 over 16 is 2.75.
Divide by 11 for the moles of hydrate: 0.25.
Mass of anhydrous zinc sulfate: 0.25 times 161 is 40.25 grams.

9ed32705-8c86-42d5-a6c3-11c5c38aabc6.heading: Hydrogen count in a lead additive

beats.say: Lead is the rest: 100 minus 29.7 minus 6.19 is 64.11 percent.
Lead: 64.11 over 207 is 0.310.
Carbon: 29.7 over 12 is 2.475.
Hydrogen: 6.19 over 1 is 6.19.
That ratio is 1 to 8 to 20, so x is 20.
Only 15 percent efficient, so feed in enough for a theoretical 600 over 0.15: 4000 cubic decimetres.
For gases, volumes follow the mole ratio: nitrogen is 4000 over 2, which is 2000.
Hydrogen is 3 times that: 6000 cubic decimetres.

a00602eb-3335-4ea9-ba21-5d24dce55313.heading: Concentration of NaOH from a titration

beats.say: Moles of acid: 0.5 times 25 over 1000 is 0.0125 moles.
The ratio is 1 to 1, so 0.0125 moles of sodium hydroxide in 20 cubic centimetres.
Concentration: 0.0125 divided by 20 over 1000 is 0.625.

a04b657a-9229-43c9-a5ef-82ea6d50ad94.heading: Identify X in the oxide X2O5

beats.say: The mass of X is 106.5 minus 60, which is 46.5 grams.
Moles of oxygen: 60 over 16 is 3.75.
The formula has 2 X for every 5 oxygen: 3.75 times 2 over 5 is 1.50 moles of X.
Relative atomic mass: 46.5 over 1.50 is 31, which is phosphorus.

a0ca50d4-4c5b-44d5-bdf1-fcae34e772f5.heading: Sodium hydroxide to neutralise the acid

beats.say: Moles of acid are volume times concentration: 13.86 moles.
The equation is 1 to 1, so 13.86 moles of hydroxide, which means 13.86 moles of sodium hydroxide.
The Mr of sodium hydroxide is 23 plus 16 plus 1, which is 40.
Mass: 13.86 times 40 is 554 grams.
The same charge means the same moles of electrons. Silver: 54.0 over 108 is 0.500 moles.
Silver takes one electron per atom, so 0.500 moles of electrons passed.
Tin: 14.9 over 119 is 0.125 moles.
Electrons per tin atom: 0.500 over 0.125 is 4. So the ion is tin 4 plus.

a3242c87-d8b2-4e58-be9b-6c3040f5ee1f.heading: Atoms in 22 g of carbon dioxide

beats.say: The Mr of carbon dioxide is 12 plus 2 times 16, which is 44.
Moles: 22 over 44 is 0.5.
Molecules: 0.5 times 6.02 times ten to the twenty-three is 3.01 times ten to the twenty-three.
Each molecule has 1 carbon and 2 oxygens, so there are 6.02 times ten to the twenty-three oxygen atoms.
Moles of ethanol: 23 over 46 is 0.5 moles.
So the theoretical bromoethane is 0.5 moles.
Theoretical mass: 0.5 times 109 is 54.5 grams.
Percentage yield: 27 over 54.5, times 100, is about 50 percent.

a50ea1f7-e55b-4310-b200-7131c03ed1c2.heading: Nitrogen from burning ammonia in oxygen

beats.say: Check which reactant runs out first. 200 cubic centimetres of ammonia would need 200 times 3 over 4: 150 of oxygen.
Only 120 is supplied, so oxygen is limiting.
Working from the oxygen: 120 times 2 over 3 is 80 cubic centimetres of nitrogen. The water is a liquid, so it adds no gas.

a52fac5c-a402-40d6-be5d-5e59675dbab5.heading: Hydrogen from magnesium and dilute acid

beats.say: Moles of magnesium: 6.0 over 24 is 0.25.
Moles of acid: 0.100 cubic decimetres times 0.10 is 0.010.
2 moles of acid react with 1 of magnesium: 0.010 moles of acid needs only 0.005 of magnesium, so the acid is limiting.
Hydrogen: 0.010 over 2 is 0.0050 moles.
Volume: 0.0050 times 24 is 0.12 cubic decimetres.
Moles of acid: 25.00 over 1000, times 0.100, is 2.50 times ten to the minus three.
It needs twice as much alkali: 5.00 times ten to the minus three moles of sodium hydroxide.
Volume: divide by 0.250, giving 0.0200 cubic decimetres.
That is 20.00 cubic centimetres.
She added 24.00, so she went past the end-point, and the excess alkali turns methyl orange yellow.

a94343ce-3a2e-4808-9e9f-f297dca3a971.heading: Empirical and molecular formula of Z

beats.say: Divide each percentage by the relative atomic mass. Carbon: 40.0 over 12 is 3.33.
Hydrogen: 6.7 over 1 is 6.7.
Oxygen: 53.3 over 16 is 3.33.
Dividing through by the smallest gives 1 to 2 to 1, so the empirical formula is CH2O.
Its mass is 12 plus 2 plus 16, which is 30.
60 over 30 is 2, so the molecular formula is twice the empirical one.
Moles of acid: 1.2 over 88 is 0.01364 moles.
The ratio is 1 to 1, so in theory 0.01364 moles of ester.
Theoretical mass: 0.01364 times 116 is 1.58 grams.
Percentage yield: 0.75 over 1.58, times 100, is 47.4 percent.

a9faffd2-d774-4a0f-a4b2-2201c9e5988e.heading: Iron(III) oxide for 53.5 g of iron(III) hydroxide

beats.say: The Mr of iron(III) hydroxide is 56 plus 3 lots of 16 plus 1, which is 107.
Moles: 53.5 over 107 is 0.500.
Step II is 1 to 1, so 0.500 moles of iron(III) nitrate.
Step I gives 2 iron(III) nitrate from each iron(III) oxide, so halve it: 0.250 moles.
The Mr of iron(III) oxide is 160.
Mass: 0.250 times 160 is 40 grams.
Moles of carbon dioxide: 18 over 24 is 0.75.
2 moles of XO give 1 mole of carbon dioxide: 2 times 0.75 is 1.5 moles.
Mr of XO: 120 over 1.5 is 80.
Subtract the oxygen: 80 minus 16 is 64.
The Mr of propanol is 60, so 8 grams is 8 over 60: 0.1333 moles.
The equation is 1 to 1, so the theoretical yield is 0.1333 moles of bromopropane.
Its Mr is 36 plus 7 plus 80, which is 123.
Theoretical mass: 0.1333 times 123 is 16.4 grams.
Percentage yield: 10 over 16.4, times 100, is 61.0 percent.

aaf9f290-a89e-4a17-be21-645553795694.heading: Relative atomic mass of Y from its nitrate

beats.say: Moles of gas: 1.8 over 24 is 0.075.
From the equation, 2 moles of the nitrate give 3 moles of gas: 0.075 times 2 over 3 is 0.05.
Mr of the nitrate: 8.5 over 0.05 is 170.
Take away the nitrogen and three oxygens: 170 minus 14 minus 48 is 108.
Find the mass of pure dolomite that made the gas. Carbon dioxide: 0.45 over 44 is 0.01023 moles.
Each dolomite has two carbonate groups, so it gives 2 moles of carbon dioxide: halve it.
Its Mr is 40 plus 24 plus 2 times 60, which is 184.
Mass of pure dolomite: 0.005114 times 184 is 0.941 grams.
Purity: 0.941 out of 2.00 grams, times 100, is 47.1 percent.
The Mr of zinc carbonate is 125, so 125 grams is exactly 1 mole.
That would give 1 mole of zinc oxide.
Zinc oxide has Mr 81, so the theoretical mass is 81 grams.
Percentage yield: 75 over 81, times 100.

b0e2c487-42a9-4efc-a439-90b477741d70.heading: Gases left after oxygen meets sulfur dioxide

beats.say: Volumes react in the ratio 1 to 2 to 2. 20 cubic centimetres of sulfur dioxide needs only 10 of oxygen.
It forms 20 cubic centimetres of sulfur trioxide; the sulfur dioxide is limiting and all used up.
Oxygen left: 40 minus 10 is 30 cubic centimetres.
Moles of iron(II) carbonate: 150 over 116.
The equation is 1 to 1, so the theoretical mass of iron(II) oxide is 150 over 116, times 72 grams.
Percentage yield is actual over theoretical, times 100.
Rearranging gives 50 times 116 times 100, over 150 times 72.
Moles of sodium hydroxide: 10.0 over 1000, times 3.00, is 0.0300.
Moles of the chloride: 10.0 over 1000, times 1.50, is 0.0150.
The ratio is 0.0300 to 0.0150, which is 2 to 1.
In the equation that ratio is n to 1, so n is 2: the metal forms a 2 plus ion and the chloride is MCl2.

b25f74e5-198c-4d27-8ff9-5a01e53d8438.heading: Percentage purity of iron(III) oxide in haematite

beats.say: Find the iron(III) oxide that reacted. Iron: 4700 grams over 56 is 83.93 moles.
1 mole of iron(III) oxide gives 2 of iron, so halve it: 41.96 moles.
The Mr of iron(III) oxide is 160.
Mass: 41.96 times 160 is 6714 grams, which is 6.714 kilograms.
Purity: 6.714 out of 10.00 kilograms, times 100, is 67.1 percent.

b2993c53-29bb-4b40-8ba0-8f51c0796e40.heading: Moles of X in 8 g of X2O3

beats.say: The oxide is 70 percent X, so the other 30 percent is oxygen.
Mass over 16 gives the moles of oxygen atoms: 2.4 over 16.
The formula fixes X to O as 2 to 3, so take two thirds of the oxygen moles.

b2dd1a39-4ebc-433e-be30-7b695ce4c323.heading: Mass of 2 moles of chlorine gas

beats.say: Chlorine gas is diatomic, Cl2, so its Mr is 2 times 35.5, which is 71.
Moles times Mr gives the mass: 2 times 71 is 142 grams.
Take each percentage as grams and divide by the Ar. Nitrogen: 63.6 over 14 is 4.54.
Oxygen: 36.4 over 16 is 2.28.
Divide both by the smaller, 2.28: nitrogen to oxygen is 2 to 1, so the formula is N2O.

b567cb3c-1980-4b48-80e2-ccf3a40d1dfc.heading: Which gives the most magnesium nitrate?

beats.say: Turn each mass into moles. Magnesium: 36 over 24 is 1.5 moles.
Magnesium oxide: 40 over 40 is 1.0 mole.
Magnesium carbonate: 42 over 84 is 0.5 moles.
Each gives 1 mole of magnesium nitrate per mole, so reaction 1, with 1.5 moles, gives the most.

b5741211-5000-42ea-9581-d8bfffdc0884.heading: Volume of 0.1 mol/dm³ HCl for 25 cm³ of Na2CO3

beats.say: Moles of sodium carbonate: 0.2 times 25 over 1000 is 0.005 moles.
That is 0.005 moles.
The equation needs 2 HCl for each sodium carbonate, so double it: 0.010 moles.
Volume is moles over concentration: 0.010 over 0.1 is 0.1 cubic decimetres.
That is 100 cubic centimetres.

b6a9550d-b790-4d48-890a-35f7d64661b3.heading: Hydrocarbon X from its gas volumes

beats.say: By Avogadro, gas volume ratios are mole ratios. 3 cubic centimetres of CO2 from 1 means 3 carbon atoms, so x is 3.
The combustion uses x plus y over 4 moles of oxygen. With 4 of oxygen, 3 plus y over 4 equals 4.
So y over 4 is 1, and y is 4. X is C3H4.
21.0 grams of sodium hydrogencarbonate over its Mr of 84 is 0.250 moles.
The equation is 2 to 1, so that would give 0.125 moles of sodium carbonate.
Times its Mr of 106: a theoretical mass of 13.25 grams.
The percentage yield is the actual 10.6 grams over that figure, times 100. That is option D written out.

b6e3743f-e838-4737-97d1-e6b2c5ff7aab.heading: Citric acid in lemon juice, in g/dm³

beats.say: Moles of sodium hydroxide: 29.50 over 1000, times 0.55, is 0.01623 moles.
That is 0.01623 moles.
Citric acid is tribasic, so each mole needs 3 moles of alkali. Divide by 3: 0.005408 moles.
Over the 0.0250 cubic decimetres of juice: 0.2163 moles per cubic decimetre.
Times the molar mass, 192, gives 41.5 grams per cubic decimetre. 0.216 is the trap in option A.

b733e252-a66e-4c6a-8fe2-b6b0a8fda313.heading: C=C bonds in a vegetable oil molecule

beats.say: Each C=C bond adds exactly one molecule of bromine. Moles of bromine: 19.2 over 160 is 0.12.
There are 0.02 moles of oil, so each molecule takes 0.12 over 0.02, which is 6 bromines: 6 C=C bonds.

b7f937e0-4ac6-4881-882e-58cb8bdf8298.heading: Gas left after burning ammonia, then carbon

beats.say: 40 cubic centimetres of ammonia needs 40 times 3 over 4, which is 30, of oxygen.
So of the 50 of oxygen, 20 is left over.
It makes 40 times 2 over 4, which is 20, of nitrogen. The water is liquid.
In reaction 2 the remaining 20 of oxygen becomes 20 of carbon dioxide.
Final mixture: 20 of nitrogen plus 20 of carbon dioxide is 40 cubic centimetres.

b99dbbcf-b978-49fa-ba6b-1f8b26288c62.heading: Oxygen needed for 102 g of aluminium oxide

beats.say: 102 grams of aluminium oxide over its Mr of 102 is 1 mole.
2 moles of aluminium oxide need 3 moles of oxygen, so 1 mole needs 1.5 moles.
Times 24 cubic decimetres per mole at r.t.p.: 36 cubic decimetres.

bc9e0cc9-3cc2-42b5-82c9-27da97b1d4fb.heading: Nickel atoms in a 10.0 g coin

beats.say: Nickel is 20.0 percent of 10.0 grams: 2.00 grams.
Over its Ar of 59: 0.0339 moles.
Times the Avogadro constant, 6.0 times ten to the twenty-three, gives 2.03 times ten to the twenty-two atoms.

bcae407a-33ab-44a9-a784-56ab2161f2c9.heading: Which alkane needs 130 cm³ of O2 for 20 cm³?

beats.say: Equal volumes of gas hold equal moles, so alkane to oxygen is 20 to 130, which is 1 to 6.5.
An alkane with n carbons needs 3n plus 1, over 2, moles of oxygen. Set that equal to 6.5.
So 3n plus 1 is 13, and n is 4: butane, C4H10.
Check with the equation: 2 to 13 is 1 to 6.5.

bd9ec804-baef-4589-aab6-e86bc5f9bb98.heading: Oxygen used to burn 50 cm³ of ethane

beats.say: At the same temperature and pressure, volumes go as the mole ratio: ethane to oxygen is 2 to 7.
So 50 cubic centimetres of ethane needs 50 times 7 over 2, which is 175 cubic centimetres of oxygen.

be042386-3bf7-498c-95fc-7e9cbf189504.heading: 6 g of ethane: which statement is wrong?

beats.say: Ethane has an Mr of 30, so 6 grams is 0.2 moles.
That holds 0.2 times 6, which is 1.2 moles of hydrogen atoms, so A and B are right.
Times 24 gives the volume: 4.8 cubic decimetres, not 0.25. So D is incorrect.

bec7810a-9249-4626-be9e-343bbbb02958.heading: 20 dm³ of H2 with 30 dm³ of Cl2 at 100 °C

beats.say: By volume, hydrogen to chlorine to hydrogen chloride is 1 to 1 to 2.
20 of hydrogen reacts with 20 of chlorine to give 40 of hydrogen chloride.
That leaves 30 minus 20, which is 10 cubic decimetres of chlorine in excess.
At 100 degrees everything is a gas, so the total is 40 plus 10: 50 cubic decimetres.

bf0fb3c4-a683-41b6-b03c-e806350ea14b.heading: Making a 2 mol/dm³ salt solution from X

beats.say: Solution X: 0.1 moles in 0.100 cubic decimetres is 1 mole per cubic decimetre.
For 2 moles per cubic decimetre, the same 0.1 moles must sit in 0.1 over 2, which is 0.05 cubic decimetres.
That is 50 cubic centimetres, so 50 cubic centimetres of water must be evaporated.
Moles of sodium hydroxide: 0.200 times 75 over 1000 is 0.0150.
Moles of sulfuric acid: 0.200 times 25 over 1000 is 0.00500.
The acid is dibasic, so it needs 2 times 0.00500, which is 0.0100 moles of sodium hydroxide.
Excess sodium hydroxide: 0.0150 minus 0.0100 is 0.00500 moles.
The total volume is 100 cubic centimetres, which is 0.100 cubic decimetres.
Concentration: 0.00500 over 0.100 is 0.0500 moles per cubic decimetre.

c0cedd47-d9b7-4831-868f-10aa380283af.heading: Percentage of NaHCO3 from the loss in mass

beats.say: The mass lost is the carbon dioxide and the water. 2 moles of sodium hydrogencarbonate is 168 grams.
It loses 44 plus 18, which is 62 grams.
A 2.25 gram loss means 2.25 times 168 over 62, which is 6.10 grams of sodium hydrogencarbonate.
Over the 9.0 gram mixture, times 100: 67.7 percent, about 68 percent.

c183f83a-8cb3-4485-8697-b0c7a078deba.heading: Gas left from 200 cm³ SO2 and 200 cm³ O2

beats.say: From the equation, 200 cubic centimetres of sulfur dioxide needs only 100 of oxygen.
So 200 minus 100, which is 100 of oxygen, is left over.
The 200 of sulfur dioxide makes 200 of sulfur trioxide.
Total gas left: 200 plus 100 is 300 cubic centimetres.

c2058658-bab4-4f36-a5e0-6719d47f1104.heading: 10 g CaCO3 with 100 cm³ of 1 mol/dm³ HCl

beats.say: Calcium carbonate: 10 over 100 is 0.100 moles.
Acid: 100 over 1000, times 1, is 0.100 moles.
