The equation needs 2 acid per carbonate, so 0.100 moles of carbonate would need 0.200. The acid is limiting.
Carbon dioxide is half the acid: 0.0500 moles, times 24 is 1.20 cubic decimetres. Statement 1 is right.
Calcium chloride is also 0.0500 moles, times 111 is 5.55 grams. Statement 2 is right.
Carbon dioxide weighs 0.0500 times 44, which is 2.2 grams, not 4.80. And half the carbonate is left over.

c2b749d8-183a-48d7-8812-d9eb3f82e58b.heading: Ions left after mixing AgNO3 and NaI

beats.say: Silver ions: 0.10 times 50.0 over 1000 is 0.0050 moles.
Iodide ions: 0.05 times 150.0 over 1000 is 0.0075 moles.
They react 1 to 1, so all the silver is precipitated and 0.0025 moles of iodide is left over.
Sodium and nitrate stay in solution throughout, with the excess iodide, but no silver.

c3685ebb-6a4f-47ee-997b-82f8034e559d.heading: NaOH needed to remove 0.02 mol of N2O5

beats.say: The equation needs 2 sodium hydroxide for every N2O5: 2 times 0.02 is 0.04 moles.
Volume is moles over concentration: 0.04 over 0.8 is 0.05 cubic decimetres.
That is 50.0 cubic centimetres.

c44216d6-596e-41fc-b1c0-48d9e46ae574.heading: Percentage purity of chalk from CO2 volume

beats.say: Moles of carbon dioxide: 5.42 over 24 is 0.226.
The equation is 1 to 1, so there were 0.226 moles of calcium carbonate.
Times 100: 22.6 grams.
Over the 23.0 grams of chalk, times 100: 98.2 percent pure.

c48af3db-14bb-4526-8f2f-7c573ed2b374.heading: 2.4 g Mg with 100 cm³ of 1 mol/dm³ HCl

beats.say: Magnesium: 2.4 over 24 is 0.100 moles.
Acid: 100 over 1000, times 1, is 0.100 moles.
The equation needs 2 acid per magnesium, so 0.100 moles of magnesium would need 0.200. The acid is limiting.
Hydrogen is half the acid: 0.0500 moles, times 24 is 1.2 cubic decimetres. Statement 1 is right.
Magnesium chloride is also 0.0500 moles, times 95 is 4.75 grams. Statement 2 is right.
Hydrogen weighs 0.0500 times 2, which is 0.1 grams, not 0.2. And magnesium is left over.

c4c4caab-2539-4eda-8c50-c784030b8059.heading: Ammonia from 0.75 mol of H2 at 30 % yield

beats.say: Nitrogen is in excess, so hydrogen decides. 3 moles of hydrogen give 2 of ammonia.
The yield is only 30 percent: 0.50 times 30 over 100 is 0.15 moles.
Times 24 gives 3.6 cubic decimetres.
That is 3600 cubic centimetres. 12000 is the trap: the 100 percent yield figure.

c4d47cb7-d493-4cb1-bc52-87ee57d7d9d6.heading: Concentration of 31.5 g HNO3 in 200 cm³

beats.say: The Mr of nitric acid: 1 plus 14 plus 3 times 16 is 63.
Moles: 31.5 over 63 is 0.5.
The volume is 200 over 1000, which is 0.2 cubic decimetres.
Concentration: 0.5 over 0.2 is 2.5 moles per cubic decimetre.

c5ea2a73-9842-45e7-ade5-457593f4460d.heading: Purity of sodium carbonate by back titration

beats.say: Total acid added: 0.500 times 35.0 over 1000 is 0.01750 moles.
The excess equals the sodium hydroxide: 0.400 times 15.0 over 1000 is 0.00600 moles.
Acid that reacted with the carbonate: 0.01750 minus 0.00600 is 0.01150 moles.
Sodium carbonate takes 2 acid each, so halve it: 0.00575 moles.
Times 106 gives 0.610 grams.
Over the 1.41 gram sample, times 100: 43.2 percent pure.

c69116f8-30a0-4f46-9326-4cd1f75ade18.heading: Hydrogen ions in 50 cm³ of 1 mol/dm³ H2SO4

beats.say: Moles of sulfuric acid: 1 times 50 over 1000 is 0.050.
Sulfuric acid is dibasic, releasing 2 hydrogen ions per molecule: 2 times 0.050 is 0.100 moles.

c6b38e5a-e607-4c0f-88a5-b60e4358bfc0.heading: Gas volume after 10 % of O2 becomes ozone

beats.say: 10 percent of 150 is 15 cubic centimetres of oxygen that reacts.
3 oxygen give 2 ozone, so 15 of oxygen gives 10 of ozone.
Unreacted oxygen: 150 minus 15 is 135.
Total: 135 plus 10 is 145 cubic centimetres.
Moles of manganese: 110 over 55 is 2.0.
Moles of fluorine: 72 over 24 is 3.0.
Manganese to fluorine is 2 to 3, which matches option C.

c8cbe0aa-3b3b-4ea1-b7e5-7a0309558d89.heading: Gas from burning one mole of C6H12O6

beats.say: One mole of the carbohydrate gives 6 moles of carbon dioxide and 6 of water.
At room temperature and pressure water is a liquid, so only the carbon dioxide is collected: 6 times 24 is 144.
Counting the water as a gas too would give 288, which is the trap.

c8d77a00-e576-4d07-bdc0-08cb5f492bc2.heading: 4 g of H2 ignited with 16 g of O2

beats.say: 4 grams of hydrogen is 2 moles.
16 grams of oxygen is 0.5 moles.
Oxygen is limiting: 0.5 moles of oxygen reacts with 1 mole of hydrogen.
That leaves 1 mole, which is 2 grams, of hydrogen unreacted.
And it makes 1 mole of water, 18 grams. Left: 2 grams of hydrogen, no oxygen, 18 grams of water.

c8ecd5b8-9a7e-4095-90de-063a027b9020.heading: Sulfuric acid to neutralise 100 cm³ of NaOH

beats.say: Moles of sodium hydroxide: 100 over 1000, times 1.0, is 0.10.
The equation needs half as many moles of acid: 0.050 moles of sulfuric acid.
Option B supplies 50 over 1000, times 1.0, which is 0.050 moles: exactly what is needed.

ca525a2d-950e-4944-af5b-e91e44445ea1.heading: Mass of C7H12O that decolourises 0.5 mol Br2

beats.say: The saturated alcohol with 7 carbons has 4 more hydrogen atoms, so this one has two C=C bonds.
Each C=C reacts with one bromine, so 1 mole of alcohol reacts with 2 moles of bromine.
0.5 moles of bromine needs 0.25 moles of alcohol.
Times the Mr of 112: 28 grams.

ca539daa-dccb-45e7-beae-a848e480be21.heading: Moles of Y in 1.4 g, from Y2O5

beats.say: In 5.4 grams of the oxide, the oxygen is 5.4 minus 1.4, which is 4.0 grams.
Moles of oxygen atoms: 4.0 over 16.
The formula fixes Y to O as 2 to 5, so take two fifths of the oxygen moles.
Moles of vanadium: 76.5 over 51 is 1.5.
4.5 moles of electrons deposited it: 4.5 over 1.5 is 3 electrons per ion, so the charge is 3 plus.

cc686b20-ab4e-4a6f-8bd6-143c102f0b4c.heading: Sodium ions in 30 g of sodium sulfate

beats.say: The Mr of sodium sulfate: 46 plus 32 plus 64 is 142.
Moles: 30 over 142 is 0.2113.
Each formula unit has two sodium ions: 2 times 0.2113 is 0.4225 moles.
Times the Avogadro constant, 6.02 times ten to the twenty-three, gives 2.54 times ten to the twenty-three ions.

ccb02fc9-2b76-4b1d-8e61-46b00ac50137.heading: Silver chloride from 4.08 g of zinc chloride

beats.say: The Mr of zinc chloride: 65 plus 2 times 35.5 is 136.
Moles: 4.08 over 136 is 0.0300.
The equation gives 2 silver chloride per zinc chloride: 0.0600 moles.
The Mr of silver chloride: 108 plus 35.5 is 143.5.
Mass: 0.0600 times 143.5 is 8.61 grams.

cdac1f05-b90b-440b-b5a2-235ac53388ce.heading: LiOH to neutralise the products of SO2Cl2

beats.say: 0.25 moles of SO2Cl2 would need 0.50 moles of water, and 1.0 is there, so SO2Cl2 is limiting.
It makes 0.25 moles of sulfuric acid and 0.50 moles of hydrochloric acid.
The dibasic sulfuric acid needs 2 times 0.25, which is 0.50 moles of lithium hydroxide.
The hydrochloric acid needs 0.50 moles. Total: 0.50 plus 0.50 is 1.00 mole.

ce32049d-4446-4f42-bc6f-a3a35be575db.heading: C=C bonds from the hydrogen a fat takes up

beats.say: Each C=C double bond adds exactly one molecule of hydrogen. Moles of oil: 5 over 800 is 0.00625.
Moles of hydrogen: 900 over 24000 is 0.0375.
Double bonds per molecule: 0.0375 over 0.00625 is 6.
Urea has an Mr of 60, so 0.120 grams is 0.002 moles.
The sodium hydroxide absorbs the carbon dioxide, leaving only nitrogen: 2 moles per mole of urea.
Times 24000 cubic centimetres per mole: 96.0 cubic centimetres.
125 grams of zinc carbonate over its Mr of 125 is 1 mole.
That gives a theoretical 1 mole of zinc oxide, which is 81 grams.
The yield is the actual 75 grams over 81, times 100.
(CH2O)6 is C6H12O6. 0.50 moles of it gives 0.50 times 6, which is 3.0 moles of carbon dioxide.
The water is a liquid at room temperature and pressure, so it is not collected. Volume: 3.0 times 24 is 72.
Mass divided by the relative atomic mass: 0.13 over 13 is 0.010 moles of carbon-13.
Carbon has 6 protons, so each carbon-13 atom has 13 minus 6, which is 7 neutrons.
Moles of neutrons: 0.010 times 7 is 0.07 moles.
So the number of neutrons is 0.07 times the Avogadro constant.

d1889ccc-1934-4030-b2a3-035760f5cc0c.heading: Moles of X in the oxide X2O5

beats.say: The oxide is 10.2 grams and 5.4 grams of it is X, so the oxygen is 10.2 minus 5.4, which is 4.8 grams.
Moles of oxygen atoms: 4.8 divided by 16.
In X2O5 the ratio of X to O is 2 to 5, so multiply by 2 over 5.
Using 10.2 would be wrong: that total mass is not all one element.

d1e39b60-846f-4cc0-a405-08ef24aee204.heading: Gas from burning 0.5 mol of ethane

beats.say: The equation says 2 moles of ethane give 4 moles of carbon dioxide, so 0.5 moles of ethane gives 1 mole.
At room temperature and pressure water is a liquid, so the only gaseous product is carbon dioxide.
One mole of gas is 24 cubic decimetres, so 1 times 24 is 24 cubic decimetres.

d1fd190c-88f4-4564-9dde-b5eb1e9214c1.heading: Ammonium nitrate from 17 kg of ammonia

beats.say: Stage 1 uses one ammonia to make the nitric acid, and stage 2 uses a second ammonia to neutralise it. So 2 moles of ammonia make 1 mole of ammonium nitrate.
Moles of ammonia: 17 kilograms over 17 is 1 kilomole.
Halve it for the 2 to 1 ratio: 0.5 kilomoles of ammonium nitrate.
Moles times Mr: 0.5 times 80 is 40 kilograms.

d37faa9a-5dcc-4182-8ebb-adf3f9f01149.heading: Hydrogen to harden 75 g of fat

beats.say: First count the double bonds from the bromine data. Moles of fat: 150 over 300 is 0.500 moles.
Moles of bromine: 240 over 160 is 1.50 moles.
1.50 over 0.500 is 3, so each fat molecule has 3 double bonds.
Now the smaller sample: 75 over 300 is 0.250 moles of fat.
Hydrogen adds one molecule per double bond, just like bromine: 3 times 0.250 is 0.750 moles.
Volume: 0.750 times 24 is 18 cubic decimetres.

d4180998-6cf5-47ec-881e-a66008e2e06b.heading: Formula of the sulfate of M

beats.say: Moles of hydroxide: 10 over 1000, times 2.0, is 0.0200 moles.
Moles of sulfuric acid: 50 over 1000, times 0.20, is 0.0100 moles.
The ratio is 2 to 1, so 2 MOH react with 1 sulfuric acid.
M forms M plus, and two M plus ions balance one sulfate ion: M2SO4.

d4ea7b5b-f5ec-47bb-8254-2a1a1b57120e.heading: Charge on chromium from the same charge

beats.say: Copper: 4 over 64 is 0.0625 moles.
Each copper 2 plus ion takes 2 electrons, so 0.125 moles of electrons.
Chromium: 2.17 over 52 is 0.0417 moles.
The same charge means the same moles of electrons: 0.0417 n equals 0.125, so n is 3.
Moles of calcium oxide: 8.00 over 56 is 0.1429 moles.
The equation gives 1 mole of salt per mole of oxide, so the theoretical yield is 0.1429 moles.
Mr of calcium nitrate: 40 plus 2 times 14 plus 48, which is 164.
Theoretical mass: 0.1429 times 164 is 23.4 grams.
Percentage yield: 12.65 over 23.4, times 100, is 54.0 percent.
Mr of magnesium sulfate: 24 plus 32 plus 64 is 120.
Moles: 1.20 over 120 is 0.01 moles.
Mr of magnesium hydroxide: 24 plus 32 plus 2 is 58.
One mole of magnesium sulfate gives one mole of magnesium hydroxide, so the theoretical mass is 0.01 times 58, which is 0.58 grams.
Percentage yield: 0.32 over 0.58, times 100, is 55.2 percent.
The equation says 5 moles of HCl come from 1 mole of PCl5. So 3 moles of HCl came from 3 over 5, which is 0.6 moles.
Mr of PCl5: 31 plus 5 times 35.5 is 208.5.
Mass of pure PCl5: 0.6 times 208.5 is 125.1 grams.
Purity: 125.1 out of 130, times 100, is 96.2 percent.
Moles of sodium: 46 over 23 is 2.0 moles.
The equation shows 2 moles of sodium go with 1 mole of chlorine, so halve it: 1.0 mole.
Mr of the hydrated crystals: 40, plus 2 times 35.5, plus 6 times 18, is 219.
Moles: 54.75 over 219 is 0.25 moles.
The mole ratio hydrated to anhydrous is 1 to 1, so 0.25 moles of calcium chloride.
Calcium chloride has Mr 111: 0.25 times 111 is 27.75, about 27.8 grams.

dada3e89-7abe-432d-83df-bb4bb69dbe42.heading: Empirical formula of the lead additive

beats.say: Lead makes up the rest: 100 minus 29.7 minus 6.2 is 64.1 percent.
Divide by the relative atomic mass. Lead: 64.1 over 207 is 0.3097.
Carbon: 29.7 over 12 is 2.475. Hydrogen: 6.2 over 1 is 6.2.
Divide through by the smallest, 0.3097: lead 1, carbon 7.99, hydrogen 20.0.
So the formula is PbC8H20, and x is 20.

db82bd55-f678-4d78-a9cc-31519c850f07.heading: Most silver chloride from the mixture

beats.say: The hydrochloric acid is the limiting reagent: 0.05 cubic decimetres times 0.1 is 0.005 moles.
So 0.005 moles of silver chloride form.
Mass: 0.05 times 0.1 times 143.5 grams.

dbb57801-b8e7-4f40-b8a1-e7307cdd064b.heading: Gas left after burning 20 cm³ of propene

beats.say: 20 cubic centimetres of propene uses 9 over 2 times 20, which is 90 cubic centimetres of oxygen.
Oxygen left: 500 minus 90 is 410 cubic centimetres.
Carbon dioxide formed: 6 over 2 times 20 is 60 cubic centimetres.
The water is a liquid at room temperature, so it adds no gas volume.
Total: 410 plus 60 is 470 cubic centimetres.
Moles of bromoethane: 10.90 over 109 is 0.100 moles.
The equation is 1 to 1, so the theoretical yield is 0.100 moles of ethanol.
Theoretical mass: 0.100 times 46 is 4.60 grams.
Percentage yield: 3.45 over 4.60, times 100, is 75 percent.
20 cubic centimetres of methanethiol would need 60 of oxygen, but only 30 is there, so oxygen is limiting.
30 cubic centimetres of oxygen reacts with 10 of methanethiol.
That leaves 20 minus 10, which is 10 cubic centimetres of methanethiol unreacted.
It makes 10 cubic centimetres of carbon dioxide and 10 of sulfur dioxide. The water is a liquid once cooled.
Total gas: 10 plus 10 plus 10 is 30 cubic centimetres.
Moles of water: 10.8 over 18 is 0.6 moles.
XCl2 to water is 0.1 to 0.6, which is 1 to 6.
So the salt is XCl2.6H2O, and n is 6.

dc89e9b1-ae74-4b09-9773-067bf19449f7.heading: Volumes of 2 g of hydrogen and 16 g of methane

beats.say: Moles of hydrogen: 2 over 2 is 1 mole.
Moles of methane: 16 over 16 is 1 mole.
Equal moles of any gas take equal volumes at the same temperature and pressure, so the ratio is 1 to 1.

dd539331-2a15-4565-9f6b-c5eae97fbd02.heading: Empirical formula of the acid W

beats.say: Divide each percentage by the relative atomic mass. Carbon: 35.8 over 12 is 2.98.
Hydrogen: 4.5 over 1 is 4.5. Oxygen: 59.7 over 16 is 3.73.
Divide through by the smallest: 1 to 1.51 to 1.25.
Multiply by 4 for whole numbers: 4 to 6 to 5. The formula is C4H6O5.
Moles of carbon dioxide: 4.49 over 24 is 0.187 moles.
Carbonate and carbon dioxide are 1 to 1, so 0.187 moles of calcium carbonate.
Mass: 0.187 times 100 is 18.7 grams.
Purity: 18.7 out of 23.0, times 100, is 81.3 percent.

de050659-823e-47e5-9063-214c644da432.heading: Chlorine and hydrogen from 58.5 kg of NaCl

beats.say: 58.5 kilograms is 58500 grams. Divided by 58.5, that is 1000 moles of sodium chloride.
2 chloride ions give 1 chlorine molecule, so 500 moles of chlorine.
Mass of chlorine: 500 times 71 is 35500 grams, which is 35.5 kilograms.
2 hydrogen ions take 2 electrons to give 1 hydrogen molecule, so 500 moles of hydrogen too.
Mass of hydrogen: 500 times 2 is 1000 grams, which is 1 kilogram.
Divide each percentage by the relative atomic mass. Carbon: 28.6 over 12 is 2.38.
Hydrogen: 4.8 over 1 is 4.8. Nitrogen: 66.6 over 14 is 4.76.
Divide through by the smallest, 2.38: 1 to 2 to 2. The empirical formula is CH2N2.
Its mass is 12 plus 2 plus 28, which is 42.
126 over 42 is 3, so the molecular formula is three times the empirical formula: C3H6N6.

e0693976-b451-459f-a060-cca2abeb2fa7.heading: Residue from heating 0.2 mol of silver nitrate

beats.say: Only the silver stays behind. The nitrogen dioxide and oxygen both escape as gases.
The equation gives 2 moles of silver for 2 moles of silver nitrate, a 1 to 1 ratio, so 0.2 moles of silver.
Moles times 108 gives the mass: 0.2 times 108 is 21.6 grams.

e095f5c2-4819-42c0-bf40-92ea4f2311c4.heading: Charge on a titanium ion from 24 g and 2 mol e⁻

beats.say: First the moles of titanium deposited: 24 divided by 48 is 0.50 moles.
That 0.50 moles was deposited by 2 moles of electrons, so each titanium atom took 2 over 0.50, which is 4 electrons.
Each ion gained 4 electrons, so it carried a 4 plus charge.

e2171f89-6d05-42f9-8e33-22d444551410.heading: Relative atomic mass of X in XCl₂

beats.say: Moles of sodium hydroxide: 20.0 over 1000, times 0.500, is 0.0100 moles.
That is 0.0100 moles.
Forming X(OH)2 needs two hydroxides per X, so 0.00500 moles of XCl2 reacted.
Its Mr is the mass over the moles: 1.36 over 0.00500 is 272.
Take away the two chlorines, 71, and X is 201.

e2d7268c-3b4d-44d9-b0e5-7d6eaabac242.heading: Volume of 2.0 mol/dm³ HCl for 25.0 cm³ of LiOH

beats.say: Moles of lithium hydroxide: 1.0 times 25.0 over 1000 is 0.0250 moles.
The equation is 1 to 1, so moles of hydrochloric acid are also 0.0250.
Volume is moles over concentration: 0.0250 divided by 2.0 is 0.0125 cubic decimetres.
In cubic centimetres that is 12.5.

e301271c-65fe-42f4-bb3d-9d57f417d042.heading: Percentage of calcium in bone from 42.0 g CaO

beats.say: All the calcium ends up in the calcium oxide, so find what fraction of it is calcium. Its Mr is 40 plus 16, which is 56.
The calcium in 42.0 grams of oxide is 42.0 times 40 over 56, which is 30.0 grams.
That came from 100 grams of bone, so the percentage is 30.0 percent. 42.0 percent is the oxide, which is the trap.

e33aa574-3f66-4757-bd09-f0bd213962e9.heading: Concentration after mixing two HCl solutions

beats.say: Moles of acid in each: 0.250 times 3.00 is 0.750, and 0.350 times 2.00 is 0.700.
Together that is 1.450 moles.
The total volume is 250 plus 350, which is 600 cubic centimetres, or 0.600 cubic decimetres.
Concentration is moles over volume: 1.450 over 0.600 is 2.42. Averaging gives 2.50, which ignores the volumes.

e35e96f8-b092-47c6-b712-974de99ce9e5.heading: HCl to react with the residue from 105 g NaHCO₃

beats.say: The residue is the sodium carbonate. First the Mr of sodium hydrogen carbonate: 84.
Moles: 105 over 84 is 1.25 moles.
2 moles of it give 1 mole of sodium carbonate, so halve it: 0.625 moles.
The residue reacts with 2 moles of hydrochloric acid per mole, so 2 times 0.625 is 1.25 moles of acid.
Volume is moles over concentration: 1.25 over 0.50 is 2.50 cubic decimetres.

e4090b03-9439-4fa7-9567-c22fd30c4ed8.heading: Hydrogen from 200 cm³ of 1.0 mol/dm³ HCl

beats.say: Magnesium is in excess, so the acid decides. Moles of acid: 0.200 times 1.0 is 0.20 moles.
2 moles of acid give 1 mole of hydrogen, so 0.20 divided by 2 is 0.10 moles.
1 mole of gas takes 24 cubic decimetres at room conditions: 0.10 times 24 is 2.4.

e4808461-5e93-4a57-a302-ef202054e32d.heading: Hydrogen from 32.5 g of zinc and steam

beats.say: Moles of zinc: 32.5 divided by 65 is 0.5 moles.
Zinc to hydrogen is 1 to 1, so 0.5 moles of hydrogen.
At room conditions, 0.5 times 24 is 12 cubic decimetres.

e4c6ddb4-2748-4c9b-958c-b137426384ee.heading: 30 cm³ N₂ with 60 cm³ H₂ — what is left?

beats.say: Gas volumes react in the ratio 1 to 3 to 2. 30 of nitrogen would need 90 of hydrogen, but only 60 is there, so hydrogen runs out.
60 of hydrogen reacts with 60 over 3, which is 20 cubic centimetres of nitrogen.
It makes 2 times 20, which is 40 cubic centimetres of ammonia.
Nitrogen left is 30 minus 20, which is 10. No hydrogen is left.

e54b8a04-43c1-4461-b299-165eaafa028b.heading: 2.5 mol O₂ weighs the same as 1.0 mol SOn

beats.say: The mass of 2.5 moles of oxygen: 2.5 times 32 is 80 grams.
1.0 mole of SOn has that same mass, so its Mr is 80: 32 plus 16 n equals 80.
So 16 n is 48, and n is 3.
Moles of sodium sulfate: 25.0 over 1000, times 1.00, is 0.0250 moles.
The equation is 1 to 1, so the theoretical yield is 0.0250 moles of barium sulfate.
Its mass: 0.0250 times 233 is 5.825 grams.
Percentage yield: 5.36 over 5.825, times 100, is 92.0 percent.

e772fad8-2725-458e-9f12-1f3e180ab224.heading: Mass of C₄H₆ that takes up 0.10 mol of H₂

beats.say: C4H6 needs two molecules of hydrogen to become the alkane C4H10.
So the moles of C4H6 are 0.10 divided by 2, which is 0.050 moles.
Its Mr: 4 carbons at 12 and 6 hydrogens at 1 is 54.
Mass is 0.050 times 54, which is 2.70 grams.

e86b61cf-608a-4442-9089-0de93e30058e.heading: Which oxide of nitrogen: 0.46 g in 120 cm³

beats.say: Moles of gas: 120 over 24000 is 0.0050 moles.
Mr is mass over moles: 0.46 over 0.0050 is 92.
Try N2O4: 2 nitrogens at 14 and 4 oxygens at 16 is 92. It fits.

e9be2a65-7b7f-44fc-bc61-b18e4a43c01b.heading: Percentage yield of ammonia from 12 g of H₂

beats.say: 12 grams of hydrogen is 6 moles.
3 moles of hydrogen give 2 moles of ammonia, so 6 moles give a theoretical 4 moles.
At room conditions, 4 times 24 is 96 cubic decimetres.
Percentage yield: 84 over 96, times 100, is 87.5 percent.

ebcfbcd1-fe06-48a5-b9ce-b41bd04e9884.heading: Gas left after 10 cm³ propane burns in 70 cm³ O₂

beats.say: 10 cubic centimetres of propane needs 5 times as much oxygen, 50.
So 70 minus 50, which is 20 cubic centimetres of oxygen, is left over.
The carbon dioxide formed is 3 times 10, which is 30 cubic centimetres.
The water is a liquid at room conditions, so it adds no gas. Total gas is 30 plus 20, which is 50.
0.9 grams in 100 cubic centimetres is 9 grams in every 1000.
Divide by the relative formula mass of sodium chloride, 58.5: 9 over 58.5 is 0.154.

ec2098de-9e7d-46a5-8e6a-c9ef79f9658d.heading: Purity of H₂O₂ from 3.7 dm³ of oxygen

beats.say: Moles of oxygen: 3.7 over 24 is 0.1542 moles.
2 moles of hydrogen peroxide give 1 mole of oxygen, so double it: 0.3083 moles.
Mr of hydrogen peroxide is 34, so the pure mass is 0.3083 times 34, which is 10.5 grams.
Percentage purity: 10.5 over 24.8, times 100, is 42.3 percent.

ed4f074a-20cf-4b1b-bf50-9f775e14dc23.heading: Formula of phosphorus from equal gas volumes

beats.say: Equal volumes at the same temperature and pressure hold equal moles. 71 grams of chlorine, Mr 71, is 1.00 mole.
So 124 grams of phosphorus vapour is also 1.00 mole, and its Mr is 124.
Each phosphorus atom is 31, so 124 over 31 is 4 atoms in a molecule.

ed889ef5-0cd8-461f-becf-68500bf3862e.heading: Water to dilute 8.0 mol/dm³ HCl to 2.0

beats.say: Moles of acid: 100 over 1000, times 8.0, is 0.80 moles. Diluting does not change it.
At 2.0 moles per cubic decimetre, the final volume is 0.80 over 2.0, which is 0.40, or 400 cubic centimetres.
So 400 minus 100, which is 300 cubic centimetres of water, is added.

edd5f5eb-26d8-4ba2-bbe8-e9d4b0aeb896.heading: Which solution matches 4.0 g NaOH in 500 cm³?

beats.say: Moles of sodium hydroxide: 4.0 over 40 is 0.100 moles.
In 0.500 cubic decimetres, that is 0.200 moles per cubic decimetre.
Option C: 0.05 over 0.250 is also 0.200. The others come to 0.8, 2.0 and 0.1.

edd7dedb-012a-4a1e-a4d5-d39842be8ae9.heading: Number of ions in 13.6 g of zinc chloride

beats.say: The Mr of zinc chloride is 65 plus 2 times 35.5, which is 136.
Moles: 13.6 over 136 is 0.100 moles.
Each formula unit gives 1 zinc ion and 2 chloride ions, 3 ions, so 0.300 moles of ions.
Times the Avogadro constant, 6.02 times ten to the twenty-three, gives 1.8 times ten to the twenty-three ions.

ef322e9f-88c3-458e-90c1-20c6d312346a.heading: Silver from the charge that gave 192 g of copper

beats.say: First, the moles of copper: 192 grams divided by 64 is 3 moles.
Each copper ion takes 2 electrons, so 3 moles of copper needs 6 moles of electrons.
The same charge passes through the silver nitrate. Each silver ion takes 1 electron, so 6 moles of electrons deposit 6 moles of silver.
Moles times 108 gives the mass: 6 times 108 is 648 grams.
Moles of copper(II) nitrate: 8.0 cubic centimetres over 1000, times 1.0, is 0.0080 moles.
Moles of potassium carbonate: 6.0 over 1000, times 1.0, is 0.0060 moles.
They react 1 to 1, so potassium carbonate is limiting, and 0.0020 moles of copper(II) nitrate is left over.
The copper(II) nitrate left in solution is blue, and the copper(II) carbonate formed is a green precipitate.

f0e82e5c-1aba-4b27-b2a3-23404451a5c7.heading: Gas left after burning 50 cm³ of CO

beats.say: 2 volumes of carbon monoxide need 1 volume of oxygen, so 50 cubic centimetres of CO needs only 25 of oxygen.
So 50 minus 25, which is 25 cubic centimetres of oxygen, is left over.
Carbon dioxide forms 1 to 1 with the CO, so 50 cubic centimetres of it.
The total gas is 25 plus 50, which is 75 cubic centimetres.

f11ef22f-c916-4f35-8fcd-57f4360b47bc.heading: Purity of tin ore: 900 g gives 102 g of tin

beats.say: Start from the tin: 102 grams over 119 gives the moles of tin.
The equation is 1 to 1, so the same number of moles of tin oxide reacted.
The Mr of tin oxide is 119 plus 32, which is 151.
So the mass of pure tin oxide in the ore is 102 over 119, times 151.
Purity is the pure mass over the total mass of 900 grams, times 100 percent.

f190ba4d-3c67-424d-b30f-e16aa8d6204b.heading: Silver chloride from 3.80 g of MgCl₂

beats.say: The Mr of magnesium chloride is 24 plus 2 times 35.5, which is 95.
Moles: 3.80 divided by 95 is 0.0400 moles.
1 mole of magnesium chloride gives 2 moles of silver chloride, so 0.0800 moles.
The Mr of silver chloride is 108 plus 35.5, which is 143.5.
Mass: 0.0800 times 143.5 is 11.48 grams.

f2d78f02-c2e9-49e7-a939-d90712c72662.heading: Acid needed for 1.25 g of zinc carbonate

beats.say: The Mr of zinc carbonate is 65 plus 12 plus 48, which is 125.
Moles: 1.25 divided by 125 is 0.0100 moles.
The equation needs 2 HCl per carbonate, so 0.0200 moles of acid.
Volume is moles over concentration: 0.0200 over 1.0 is 0.0200 cubic decimetres, which is 20 cubic centimetres.

f58b4a04-adab-4523-aa2a-b99868573866.heading: Mr of gas X from a 250 cm³ flask

beats.say: The mass of the gas is the full flask minus the empty flask: 16.2850 minus 15.9516 is 0.3334 grams.
The volume is 250 cubic centimetres, which is 0.250 cubic decimetres.
At room temperature and pressure one mole of gas takes 24 cubic decimetres, so 0.250 over 24 is 0.01042 moles.
Mr is mass over moles: 0.3334 over 0.01042 is 32.

f58f3bb3-4155-4f0d-98fd-bfee8b9b43a6.heading: Purity of a 23.0 g piece of chalk

beats.say: The chalk holds 0.226 moles of calcium carbonate. Times its Mr of 100, that is 22.6 grams of pure calcium carbonate.
Purity is the pure mass over the whole piece: 22.6 over 23.0, times 100, is 98.3 percent.

f6007afd-72da-4c14-988a-db51d3e9ec2a.heading: Glucose for 50 cm³ of a 0.4 mol/dm³ solution

beats.say: Moles are concentration times volume in cubic decimetres: 0.4 times 50 over 1000 is 0.020 moles.
Mass is moles times Mr: 0.020 times 180 is 3.6 grams.

f6ac6ae5-8117-4b94-ba6c-2da01d9615f7.heading: Percentage yield of oxygen from H₂O₂

beats.say: Moles of hydrogen peroxide: 10 over 1000, times 1.0, is 0.010 moles.
Two moles of peroxide give one mole of oxygen, so the theoretical yield is 0.005 moles.
As a volume: 0.005 times 24000 is 120 cubic centimetres.
The student collected 90, so the yield is 90 over 120, times 100, which is 75 percent.

f6c1654a-289e-4961-b06d-c00b3ad130be.heading: Concentration of sulfuric acid by titration

beats.say: Moles of sodium hydroxide: 0.030 cubic decimetres times 0.1 is 0.0030 moles.
2 moles of sodium hydroxide neutralise 1 mole of sulfuric acid, so 0.0015 moles of acid.
Concentration is moles over volume: 0.0015 divided by 0.025 is 0.06 moles per cubic decimetre.
On heating the carbonate gives off carbon dioxide, so the 1.76 grams lost is carbon dioxide.
One mole of carbonate gives one mole of carbon dioxide, so 0.0400 moles of carbonate.
Mr is mass over moles: 4.00 over 0.0400 is 100.
The carbonate group accounts for 60, so the metal is 100 minus 60, which is 40: calcium.

f88f842a-f344-4db1-8067-3ffd6d8bcdff.heading: Which student had the highest yield?

beats.say: Copper(II) oxide is limiting. Its Mr is 80, the crystals' Mr is 250, and the ratio is 1 to 1, so the theoretical mass is 3.125 times the oxide's mass.
Student A: theoretical 12.5 grams, actual 10.0 grams, which is 80.0 percent.
Student B: theoretical 25.0 grams, actual 24.0 grams, which is 96.0 percent.
Student C: theoretical 37.5 grams, actual 32.0 grams, which is 85.3 percent.
Student D: theoretical 50.0 grams, actual 40.0 grams, which is 80.0 percent. B is the highest.

fa8d84a2-ac76-4712-9511-8a9a212e3aaf.heading: Hydrogen to harden 75 g of oil

beats.say: First the double bonds, from the bromine data. Moles of oil: 150 over 300 is 0.500 moles.
Moles of bromine: 240 over 160 is 1.50 moles.
So each molecule has 1.50 over 0.500, which is 3 double bonds.
Now the smaller sample: 75 over 300 is 0.250 moles of oil.
Hydrogen adds one molecule per double bond, just as bromine does, so 3 times 0.250 is 0.75 moles.
The anhydrous salt weighs 24.0 grams. Its Mr is 24 plus 32 plus 4 times 16, which is 120.
Moles of magnesium sulfate: 24.0 over 120 is 0.200 moles.
Water lost: 49.2 minus 24.0 is 25.2 grams.
Moles of water: 25.2 over 18 is 1.40 moles.
The ratio 0.200 to 1.40 is 1 to 7.
Moles of barium sulfate: 2.33 over 233 is 0.01 moles.
So there are 0.01 moles of sulfate, which is 0.96 grams.
As a percentage of the fertiliser: 0.96 over 2.50, times 100, is 38.4 percent.

fdc52334-baae-441c-9d30-39aac7aeba12.heading: Identify the nitrogen oxide from 0.10 mol

beats.say: From the water: 7.20 grams over 18 is 0.400 moles.
Each mole of oxide gives y moles of water, so 0.10 times y is 0.400, and y is 4.
From the ammonia: the acid is 200 over 1000, times 1.0, which is 0.200 moles of HCl.
Ammonia is neutralised 1 to 1, so there are 0.200 moles of ammonia.
Each mole of oxide gives x moles of ammonia, so 0.10 times x is 0.200, and x is 2. The oxide is N2O4.
The Mr of the oxide is 3 times 56 plus 4 times 16, which is 232.
So 116 grams is 116 over 232, which is 0.5 moles.
Each formula unit has 3 iron atoms, so the moles of iron are 3 times 0.5, which is 1.5 moles.
Mass: 1.5 times 56 is 84 grams.
The Mr of magnesium sulfate is 120, so 1.20 grams is 0.0100 moles.
That would give 0.0100 moles of magnesium hydroxide.
Its Mr is 58, so the theoretical mass is 0.58 grams.
Percentage yield: 0.26 over 0.58, times 100, is 44.8 percent.

ff7de894-ecf9-4357-a082-c645bd396856.heading: Ar of X from 240 cm³ of oxygen

beats.say: Moles of oxygen: 240 over 24000 is 0.0100 moles.
1 mole of oxygen comes from 2 moles of the nitrate, so 2 times 0.0100 is 0.0200 moles.
Mr is mass over moles: 3.40 over 0.0200 is 170.
The nitrate group is 14 plus 48, which is 62, so X is 170 minus 62, which is 108.
